text:
After analyzing $CLAUDIA again, my view is that the AI-native IP narrative may only just be starting to be priced in by the market.

2j5SaS7xy776qCBpyPQbZjyQSAtKiFgrwjfErthnW2ZM 

The most direct catalysts behind this rally are Elon’s public recognition of Anabology’s AI music videos and a16z co-founder Marc Andreessen’s attention to the CLAUDIA account.

First, Musk. During an interview, he said that Anabology’s AI music videos made him rethink the pace of technological progress, adding that some of these works could rank among the top 10–20 best music videos he has ever seen.

Then there is Marc Andreessen, a16z’s co-founder, who follows CLAUDIA. These are two distinct signals of attention: the former directly points to the official CLAUDIA account, while the latter reflects recognition of the creative work behind CLAUDIA.

Although a follow does not imply investment or a partnership, and Elon’s praise is not an endorsement of the token, the combination of these two developments is enough to make the market reconsider the project’s original AI influencer narrative as something broader: an AI-native entertainment narrative.

Anabology is not simply making one video and then waiting for the market to speculate. The team has continued producing AI music videos around CLAUDIA, gradually building continuity in the character’s appearance, visual style, and content output. The related works have accumulated more than 6.2 million views, suggesting that this form of AI-native content has already established a certain level of reach.

At the same time, Anabology continues to invest effort in the project. The developer has publicly expressed a commitment to keep building and continues to release new work. At the very least, this indicates sustained creative momentum behind the project, rather than a team relying solely on token price action to maintain attention.

This is what distinguishes CLAUDIA from many one-off AI Memes: it is attempting to produce content continuously around a fixed character, giving users something to remember beyond a single video—the character itself.

My analysis is that what the market may really be betting on is the transformation of AI influencers from content products into independent IP.

In the past, building a recognizable entertainment character required a production team, funding, and a lengthy development cycle. Today, AI tools can dramatically reduce the cost of producing music, visual content, and character stories, giving individual creators the opportunity to operate their own virtual personalities over time.

But lower content production costs are only the first step. The real value emerges when a character begins to build an audience and users actively follow it, share its content, create derivative works, and even help expand its fictional universe.

If this model works, AI characters will no longer be merely tools or creations in the hands of their creators. They could become entertainment IP capable of accumulating influence in their own right.

CLAUDIA’s long-term thesis is precisely this: evolving from an AI-generated character into a virtual IP with a continuous content pipeline, a recognizable identity, and community influence.

This also explains why I am paying attention to both CLAUDIA and JEANPHIL. Both point to the potential opportunity in AI influencer IP. A consistent character identity combined with continuous content output could generate more durable attention than a single viral video. CLAUDIA’s current external recognition and accumulated content make it one of the projects in this narrative worth watching more closely.

From a fundamental perspective, the positive developments we can currently confirm include the creator’s continued output, millions of views for the works, Elon’s public praise of the related content, and Marc Andreessen following the Anabology account.

These developments strengthen the project’s attention base and give the AI-native entertainment narrative more concrete support.

However, view counts do not equal a stable audience, celebrity attention does not equal a commercial partnership, and continued effort from the creator does not mean the project has established a revenue model. At the token level in particular, we still need to verify whether community growth can translate into sustained demand and whether there is a clear, sustainable mechanism for capturing value for the token.

Therefore, my view is that CLAUDIA’s narrative and external attention have strengthened significantly, but its long-term token value capture remains insufficiently validated.

There are three areas worth monitoring closely going forward.

First, can Anabology’s new work continue to break through? If subsequent releases continue to attract widespread attention, Elon’s praise could mark the beginning of sustained creative momentum rather than a one-off news event.

Second, can CLAUDIA develop influence as an independent character? The real validation signal is not another person following the account. It is whether users begin discussing the character proactively, continue watching new releases, and participate in sharing and creating derivative content.

Third, can content influence translate into token demand? If the project can connect its character, creative output, community, and token mechanism, the market will have a reason to reassess its long-term value. If that connection never materializes, the success of the IP may not translate into the token’s price.

The risks are equally clear. Competition in AI-generated content will intensify, celebrity-driven attention may fade quickly, and short-term traders may take profits after a sharp rally. If subsequent releases fail to maintain their appeal or the character never builds a stable audience, this rally may remain largely driven by expectations and sentiment.

My final judgment is this: the direct catalysts behind the rally are Elon’s praise of Anabology’s work and Marc Andreessen following the official CLAUDIA account. The deeper trading thesis is that the market is beginning to bet on AI-native characters evolving into a new form of entertainment IP.

CLAUDIA’s advantage is that it already has continuous creative output and a certain level of distribution, rather than being merely an abstract AI concept. But what determines its ultimate upside is not how many more famous names appear on the list. It is whether the character can consistently produce compelling content, build a genuine audience, and ultimately establish a connection between the development of its IP and demand for its token.

If AI-native entertainment truly becomes a new sector, the eventual winners may not be the tools that generate content most efficiently, but the characters that establish user recognition first, consistently produce compelling work, and develop cultural influence. CLAUDIA is competing for that position, but it still has a long way to go before proving itself.

Let's talk about $JEANPHIL and $CLAUDIA, and why I'm bullish on the AI Influencer + short-form video narrative.

GTBxUiw6wJdmmkCGZgRHLyYxqu1vG4KtRpeox6yDpump 
2j5SaS7xy776qCBpyPQbZjyQSAtKiFgrwjfErthnW2ZM 

First, the broader sector.

I believe AI Influencers combined with short-form video distribution could become one of the narratives worth watching in the next Meme market cycle.

The underlying logic is simple: AI is turning character creation from a high-cost, low-frequency process into a low-cost, scalable content business that can be operated continuously. In the past, building an influencer required appearance, performance, filming, editing, and long-term management. Now, creators can use AI to design characters, develop personalities, produce short videos, and even operate multiple virtual personas simultaneously.

But what really matters isn't how many characters AI can generate. It's whether those characters can consistently produce content that people want to watch, discuss, and follow.

Short-form video drives distribution, characters accumulate attention, and Memes can become a speculative vehicle for that attention in the crypto market. An AI character can build a distinctive persona through continuous video releases, participate in trending topics, create new memes, and interact with other characters, gradually evolving from a single viral clip into a recognizable IP.

Compared with traditional Memes that rely on an isolated event or a single image, these characters theoretically have the ability to continuously generate new material for distribution. If a character develops a stable audience and cultural recognition, it no longer has to rely entirely on a single viral moment to maintain attention.

If this model gains traction in the crypto market, speculation may shift beyond the next viral image toward AI characters that have already attracted genuine attention on platforms like TikTok and Instagram, can consistently produce content, and have the potential to channel that external attention on-chain.

This is why I've chosen to take a deeper look at JEANPHIL and CLAUDIA. They represent two different paths within this emerging narrative.

JEANPHIL: External traction that has already emerged.

Jean Phil is an AI-generated French male character. His blond bowl cut, curled mustache, brown houndstooth suit, and signature street-style boxing moves create a recognizable visual identity that is easy to imitate.

The character has attracted significant attention on TikTok and Instagram, generating imitations and derivative content. This demonstrates how an AI character with a distinctive persona and a simple, replicable video format can quickly capture attention on mainstream social platforms.

The logic is straightforward: the character attracts external traffic, the content inspires imitations and remixes, and that attention may eventually flow into its on-chain token.

Compared with Memes that rely solely on narratives originating within crypto, JEANPHIL already has an external source of attention. What it needs to prove next is whether that momentum can persist and whether the character's popularity can translate into sustained token demand.

CLAUDIA: From AI creation toward long-term IP development.

CLAUDIA is more focused on long-term IP development. Around Claudia, anabology has been building Claudia Gallery and proposed creating an open version of Hatsune Miku for the AI era. Related initiatives also include AI character creation tools, Agent Skills, and Claudia Local.

The Influencer mode brings this vision closer to the AI Influencer model: by continuously producing videos, maintaining a consistent character identity, and experimenting with high-frequency publishing, it aims to gradually build its own audience.

The logic is that AI lowers content production costs, continuous video output helps establish character recognition, and the character gradually accumulates an audience before attempting to convert that external attention into IP influence and on-chain interest.

Compared with JEANPHIL, CLAUDIA has greater potential in the direction of a long-term AI creator ecosystem. The goal isn't simply to make a character go viral in the short term, but to explore how an AI character can continuously produce content, build an audience, and develop into an expandable, open IP.

However, this path has a longer chain of validation. Being able to produce videos consistently doesn't mean the content will necessarily gain traction. Having creation tools doesn't guarantee the ability to build a successful character. And an open-IP vision doesn't automatically mean the token can capture the resulting value.

Although both projects fall under the broader AI Influencer narrative, their trading theses are different.

JEANPHIL is more focused on existing external traction. The key question is whether that attention can persist and translate into token demand. CLAUDIA is more focused on AI creation capabilities and long-term IP development. The key question is whether it can consistently produce compelling content and build a genuine audience.

What I'm bullish on is the shared potential behind both approaches: AI characters could evolve beyond static images into dynamic IPs that continuously produce content, participate in trending topics, build social relationships, and generate new Memes.

Of course, a compelling sector narrative doesn't mean every related token will appreciate.

We need to distinguish three separate outcomes: an AI character gaining attention, an IP building lasting influence, and a token capturing value from that influence. A character can become popular without benefiting its token. A project can have impressive creation tools without producing viral content. Even if an IP continues to grow, attention may remain entirely off-chain if the token has no meaningful connection to its development.

Therefore, what I'm really looking for isn't the first token to announce that it uses AI, but projects that have demonstrated their ability to attract external attention, consistently produce distributable content, and establish a clear connection between that attention and their tokens.

AI is the production tool, short-form video is the distribution channel, character IP is the vehicle for attention, and the token represents a separate speculative market.

When these four elements become genuinely connected, AI Influencers could evolve from a trending concept into a new Meme narrative with sustained distribution potential.

In my view, the projects most likely to break out will need a distinctive character identity, consistent content distribution, a genuine external audience, and a mechanism for translating attention into token demand. That's why I'm bullish on this direction and have chosen to take a deeper look at JEANPHIL and CLAUDIA.

Filled is an independent trading terminal built on top of Collector Crypt, specializing in limit orders and automated execution for graded trading cards.

Collector Crypt itself vaults real PSA/BGS/CGC-graded physical cards and tokenizes them as 1:1 pNFTs on Solana. Users can trade these NFTs on-chain or burn them to have the physical cards shipped to their homes.

The platform has already reached considerable scale, with reported cumulative trading volume exceeding $1 billion to $1.6 billion, more than 130,000 tokenized cards, and active gacha pack openings and secondary-market trading.

However, Filled is neither the vault operator nor responsible for card custody or shipping. It simply provides a more specialized trading interface on top of Collector Crypt's public marketplace.

It addresses several pain points in traditional card markets, including high fees, slow execution, and the need to constantly monitor listings for specific cards and grades. Although on-chain markets offer instant trading, they natively lack proper limit orders, automated buying, and terminal-level monitoring.

Filled allows users to set a maximum purchase price. Its system monitors listings on Collector Crypt and Magic Eden 24/7. After verifying on-chain that the seller still holds the card, it either automatically purchases the card on the user's behalf or immediately sends an alert so the user can buy it with one click.

USDC remains in the user's own wallet until a trade is actually executed. Cancellations are free, and Filled covers network fees, so users do not need to hold SOL.

The team has publicly stated that its next steps include callouts, recommendations, offers, and Magic Eden limit orders, with the goal of becoming the primary trading terminal for the Cards ecosystem.

One Web3 work signal worth watching right now:

AI is starting to show up inside existing functions, not only in jobs labelled “AI Engineer.”

Current roles include work around:

• Compliance AI  
• CX intelligence  
• AI compute infrastructure  
• LLM-powered wallet agents  
• machine-learning risk

That’s interesting because the shift isn’t necessarily:

“Everyone becomes an AI specialist.”

It may be:
• Compliance people work with AI systems.
• Support teams use AI for customer intelligence.
• Product teams build agent-driven experiences.
• Infrastructure teams support AI workloads.
• Risk teams evaluate models.

AI starts changing the function before it changes the job title.

That doesn’t prove every Web3 role suddenly needs AI experience.

But it’s a useful thing to watch where is AI becoming part of the actual work, rather than a separate product category.

author: zerokn0wledge_
quoted_text:
While half of CT was partying in Singapore, the rest of the timeline was arguing about whether the math behind our crypto wallets could break within months.

Not (just) because of quantum computers, but also AI's rapidly increasing capabilities.

The initial warning came from one of Ethereum's lead researchers on Wednesday.

If he's right, 6.26M BTC might be first in line to be compromised. That's 31.2% of supply, and >$500B in dollar terms, sitting in addresses with exposed keys.

However, it's important to understand that nobody has broken anything so far. But the debate around the threat vector is already moving prices and roadmaps.

Missed what's happening?

Let me explain:

Your wallet is protected by a signature scheme called ECDSA.

It rests on one assumption: nobody can work backwards from your public key to your private key.

We've known since the 90s that a large enough quantum computer breaks that assumption. The comfort was always that such a machine is still years away. 

Hence, Ethereum plans to be quantum-safe around 2029. Bitcoin (so far) has no date at all.

That was the whole debate until Tuesday.

What changed?

On the 6th of October, OpenAI published 722 math papers written by an unreleased internal model. Not all of it is verified yet, but it was enough to rattle people who do math for a living.

A day later @drakefjustin, one of the Ethereum Foundation's lead researchers, wrote:

"It is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years."

His logic: if AI can suddenly do decades of math in weeks, it might also find a shortcut that cracks wallet keys on normal hardware. No quantum computer even needed.

So he asked the industry to plan for "bunker mode". Meaning: move funds, starting with the biggest holders, to fresh addresses that have never sent a transaction.

Why fresh addresses?

Because until you spend from an address, the chain only shows a scrambled fingerprint of your public key, so there is nothing to attack.

The moment you sign a transaction, the key is public forever.

That's where the 6.26M BTC figure comes from (based on @glassnode data). Binance's cold storage is 83% exposed. Robinhood's is 100%. On Solana, every address is a public key by design.

But the most important question is: Is he right?

And the answer here might be more nuanced.

Because (as mentioned before), nobody has broken anything yet. So there is no proof.

Meanwhile, most cryptographers pushed back hard. Coinbase's head of cryptography called it "the very definition of FUD", with Ledger's CTO (not sure if that's gud or bad tho lol) and Adam Back saying the same. 

The @aztecnetwork co-founder @Zac_Aztec called it "hyperbolic" and warned that the worst reaction would be rushing into newer, less tested cryptography too quickly.

@VitalikButerin landed somewhere in the middle, (re)enforcing the point to NOT scramble to move funds today, but still take AI-driven math seriously.

Then he said the part that I personally think matters the most:

Chains have roughly two families of "post-quantum" signatures to switch to.

- Lattice-based (ML-DSA, Falcon). Compact, fast, the official standard. But built on structured math, a bit like the curves we use today.

- Hash-based (SPHINCS, XMSS). Relies on nothing but a hash function, the simplest building block we have. The catch: signatures get 30 to 120 times bigger.

Vitalik's point: if the fear is AI finding hidden structure in math, lattices are exposed to that same fear. In his view only hash-based holds up against both a quantum computer and an AI shortcut.

Okay. 

Now, let's have a look at who is doing what:

- Lattices: @NEARProtocol (live since July), Algorand, Quantus, Sui (planned), Monad (draft)

- Hash-based: Ethereum's roadmap, QRL, Zcash (targeting January), and the STARK proofs under @Starknet 

Based on Vitalik's point of view (which is not consensus btw), a chain can hence be safe against quantum computers but still sit in the group he worries about.

Zac (the above-mentioned Aztec founder) counters this, pointing out that nobody actually knows that hashes are safer from AI than curves. It's an assumption rather than a fact.

But enough about the tech side. 

Because the market (as you might have noticed) reacted too, and as so often, it bought the loudest story:

- $STRK is up 65% in a week. The catalyst was Starknet saying it is "actively considering becoming an L1" to be fully quantum-resistant by 2027. There is no proposal and no vote yet.

- $QRL, hash-based since 2018, is up 41%.

- $NEAR, which actually has post-quantum signing live on mainnet, is up 12%.

- BTC, ETH and ZEC are all down.

Announcements got paid more than shipped code tho for now.

My take:

ECDSA is most likely not breaking next month, and this week may well look like FUD in hindsight.

But every chain now has to answer how fast it can swap its cryptography if it has to. Chains where you can rotate keys without changing your address (like NEAR, @SuiNetwork, @Algorand and Starknet) have the easy path. Bitcoin, with no agreed plan and a third of supply exposed, has the hardest one.

If you want to be on the safe side, keep long-term holdings in addresses that have never signed a transaction, but don't rush it and fuck up along the way.

Some of the next things I'll watch: Aztec's security roadmap, whether or not Starknet actually migrates to an L1, and whatever comes out of the Ethereum researchers' meeting that runs through Monday.

NFA tho. DYOR.

OneKey 的官方回复来了，就是同行也这样，用户自求多福！这也揭开了冷热钱包用户协议里一个很多人没注意过的“潜规则”，大家都可以看看。

平时宣传的是钱包有多安全，真到承担赔偿责任时，协议里的保障却很有限。

按 OneKey 最新协议第 15.5 条，一般累计赔偿上限，是涉案设备或备份产品的实付价、事发前 12 个月相关服务实付费用、100 美元，三者取最高。（我还查了用户协议里的签约主体 ONEKEY LIMITED。公开周年申报表显示，截至 2025 年 12 月 9 日，它的已发行及已缴股本只有 1 港元。）

你丢的可能是几万、几十万美元，上限却可能只是设备钱或 100 美元。而且这还不是保证赔付，协议另有广泛的币损免责。

按最新协议，在法律允许的最大范围内，无论什么原因造成数字资产或其价值损失，条款都试图排除赔偿责任。（第 15.4 条）

他们给出的解释，是把其他品牌的免责和限赔条款也列出来，告诉你：这是行业惯例，大家都这么做。

可用户听到这种“行业惯例”，难免觉得最后还是得自求多福。用户自己泄露助记词、误签授权，承担自己的责任，这没什么好说的。但如果经查明，问题出在厂家的供应链、硬件、固件或官方软件，为什么用户仍可能面临不赔，或者赔偿远低于实际损失的结果？

“同行也这样”，解释了这种条款有多普遍，却没有解释这样的责任分配为什么合理。每家都在宣传自己安全，到了赔偿时，又一起拿同行的低标准作理由。

OneKey，请直接回答：如果你们自身技术过失导致用户丢币，会不会依据第 15.4 条拒赔？如果需要赔，是不是仍按第 15.5 条封顶？

注：依据 OneKey 用户协议 2026.10 版，更新日期为 2026 年 10 月 11 日。

最后再问你一个问题，就是你为什么不把 MetaMask 给列出来？

MetaMask 针对未付费的用户，它的上限是给了 25000 美元，这个你为什么不列出来呢？

Papertrade 没有真实订单簿撮合，用户赚的就是平台流动池（House Funds）赔的。平台支持 1000 倍极高杠杆且承诺零滑点，开平仓直接照搬 Hyperliquid 当前的瞬时盘口买卖价

而且Papertrade 采用逐仓模式，爆仓穿仓最多只扣光保证金，盈利却能按全额涨幅找池子提现。而且池子低于 200 万美元时，用户每亏损 1 美元，平台免费送 100 枚 $PAPER 平台代币，质押代币能永远瓜分平台手续费分红

text:
papertrade got exploited for $1.28M by 0x2025137a136bea7446deba681cbfc7cf1970840e within just 8 hours of being live.

here is the on-chain breakdown of how a clever attacker with more than $13M all time PnL and $14B volume on hyperliquid exploited @papertrade_xyz

how it works: papertrade prices every trade off hyperliquid's ETH price at that exact second. so if you can move hyperliquid's price for a few seconds, papertrade pays you for it.

that's exactly what 0x2025.. did, manipulating hyperliquid's price to move their papertrade positions into profit.

22:01 opens $200M of longs on papertrade
22:01 buys 6,055 ETH on hyperliquid, price goes up $3
22:03 closes the longs → +$168k
22:03 flips to $160M of shorts
22:03 sells 5,260 ETH on hyperliquid, price drops $3
22:04 closes the shorts → +$97k
22:04 flips long again

the exploiter repeats this pattern over and over: long on papertrade, pump the price on hyperliquid, close the longs and open shorts on papertrade, dump the ETH back on hyperliquid, close the shorts.

they won 97% of their trades
296 wins out of 305 trades
typical hold: 98 seconds
total pnl: $1.73M

then it went wrong:

23:13 opens 30 shorts on papertrade, $297M at 2507.35
23:13 sells ~6,600 ETH on hyperliquid, price drops to 2504.4

same move as before. but this time the close never goes through. the short is stuck

02:31 ETH hits 2509.95. all 30 shorts liquidated, -$450k

leaving them with $1.28m of profit.

my guess is the team blocked 0x2025's closes to stop the attack. this is a temporary fix, the underlying oracle of papertrade is still identical, and vulnerable to the exact same manipulation which anyone could re-create from a fresh wallet.

it seems papertrade needs to upgrade their oracle system from using the BBO to possibly using hyperliquid's official oracle system which is less subject to manipulation as it uses a combination of exchange's price feeds.

text:
🧵 为什么说 ZK（零知识）真正的方向，是“无知的方向”？

很多人看 ZK，看的是扩容与隐私；但如果从底层逻辑来看，ZK 的背后藏着一套极其精妙的加密哲学。

一点关于隐私、权力和无穷的思考 👇

1/ 隐私，本质上是“层级管理”的衍生品

在传统社会的逻辑里，管理者极其依赖“信息不对等”来建立权力壁垒。我知道你不知道的，所以我能控制你。

早期的 privacy coins（如 ZEC）试图在公开账本里强行开辟一条暗道。但这种“对抗式隐私”，本质上依然没有脱离旧世界的控制逻辑——它依然假设存在一个“随时准备窥探你的管理者”。

2/ 点对点的世界，本来就不需要“隐私”的概念

就像人类大脑的神经元结构一样——点对点的信号传递，彼此独立又天然相连，根本不存在“思想被窃取”的焦虑。

在一个真正去中心化的点对点网络中，如果信任机制足够完备，传统意义上的“隐匿与防范”就会失去依托。

3/ ZK 的精髓，在于“不占有”

零知识证明（Zero-Knowledge Proof）的伟大之处，在于它走向了一个全新的方向：无知的方向。

它不剥开细节，不窥探历史，甚至不需要“知道”明文，就能达成对真实性的绝对确信。它从数学层面瓦解了“占有信息即占有权力”的惯性，让信任不再建立在对隐私的剥夺上。

4/ 无知的方向，即是无穷的方向

人类发明“无穷（$\infty$）”这个符号，从来不是因为宇宙中真的存在物理意义上的无穷。自然宇宙本身或许是有限且可度量的。

所谓“无穷”，不过是人类在面对自身认知边界之外的混沌时，给“无知”贴上的标签。我们总是把未知的一切，统称为无穷。

5/ 用极简，跨越认知的汪洋

ZK 技术正是利用数学，将这种“有限与无知”压缩到了极致：

我们不需要去遍历无休无止的算力与历史状态（那代表着无穷的信息消耗），只需要一个简洁的 Proof，就能直接跨越认知的鸿沟，触达确定性。

当技术不再执着于全知全能，它才真正拥抱了无穷的可能。

💡 总结：

未来的加密叙事，绝不仅仅是“隐匿数据”，而是“无知而确信”。这才是为什么在众多的底层技术中，$STRK 的 ZK 路线依然是最值得期待的方向之一。

#Crypto #ZK #Blockchain #Philosophy

The Arbitrage Terminal is worth learning to use, no matter how much capital you have.

Maybe earning 50% APR with small capital doesn't feel that lucrative.

But learning the process now means you'll know how to scale when your capital grows.

Thanks to leverage, the 4-leg strategy through @boros_fi and CrossEx lets you access a much larger notional with only a fraction of that amount in capital.

At the current quoted rates, here's what the Arbitrage Terminal estimates over roughly 20 days:

- $10K notional per leg: ~$850 in capital, ~$24 profit
- $100K notional per leg: ~$8.5K in capital, ~$225 profit
- $500K notional per leg: ~$42.4K in capital, ~$1,100 profit

These estimates assume your perp positions are already open.

If you're opening the perp legs for the first time, entry fees reduce your profit during the first cycle.

When your Boros positions mature, you can roll into the next maturity while keeping your perp positions open.

This means you can avoid paying perp opening and closing fees again during the rollover.

You simply move from one Boros maturity to the next, locking in the spread available at that time.

Learn the process with the capital you have today.

By swapping SEISMIC’s 400-byte block summaries for 8-byte “medoids,” introducing a fast blocked dot-product (JUMPDOT), and compressing index data with DOTPACKING8 and per-term 4-bit quantization, the system answers queries up to 5.3x faster and with 3x less memory than the best alternatives on MS MARCO.

Even under tight memory (≈2 GiB), it’s still up to 1.9x faster and 3.9x smaller. Forward-index compression works for any system—KANNOLO’s footprint drops by up to 50% with zero speed loss.

Memory, not pure compute, is now the bottleneck for search. This work shows you can shrink it hard, keep microsecond latency, and even run advanced retrieval on-device.

Get the full analysis here: https://t.co/tS87254CZ5

text:
The rally in $SWOLF is not driven by a single piece of news. Instead, several factors have converged: Starknet’s wolf culture, the new trend of STRK-paired tokens, momentum in STRK itself, and the holder reward data that has already been published.

HwJyyniKKDRLXxjRSzyLtpvxzqecqrhrbcSbKRm7STNK 

The most important external catalyst behind this rally is that Starknet is considering transitioning from an Ethereum L2 to an independent L1, with the goal of achieving full quantum resistance by 2027. After this news became public on October 8, STRK surged.

The market is no longer trading just the usual L2 narrative. It is now betting on whether Starknet can gain greater technological autonomy and whether quantum-resistant security can become a new competitive advantage. However, it is important to note that this is still under consideration, and the transition plan has not been finalized.

SWOLF appeared right in this time window. It is a Solana-based memecoin built around Starknet’s wolf identity and paired with STRK for trading. STRK’s rally therefore creates two potential sources of upside for SWOLF: first, as interest in the ecosystem grows, traders start looking for smaller-cap assets connected to the same narrative; second, the STRK trading pair allows SWOLF to participate directly in this wave of ecosystem-driven speculation. However, the trading pair is simply a market structure. It does not imply official endorsement from Starknet, nor does it mean SWOLF will automatically rise whenever STRK goes up.

SWOLF’s wolf identity is not entirely fabricated from scratch. I think this could qualify as a cultural token. Starknet’s community has previously organized activities around wolf imagery, including the Wolf Pack League, and the official account has also used wolf visuals in event promotions. This gives SWOLF an existing cultural connection: it does not need to explain from zero why it represents Starknet, but can instead draw on a symbol already recognized within the community. However, a cultural connection to the community is not the same as official authorization. SWOLF remains an independent memecoin.

Another important factor is that SWOLF launched around the same time StonkFun’s STRK-paired token format was emerging. The new trading pair offers a different route from the traditional SOL-paired memecoin model, giving SWOLF an opportunity to capture speculative demand tied to the STRK ecosystem. Meanwhile, the token accumulated thousands of holders and $2.2 million in 24-hour trading volume within a single day, showing that market attention had translated into actual trading activity rather than remaining just social media discussion.

However, the most interesting part of SWOLF’s story is its published holder reward data.

The website’s reward dashboard shows that approximately 580.11K STRK has been distributed, with an estimated value of $62,939. Another 19.89M SWOLF has been distributed, valued at approximately $44,344. In addition, around $68.64 in rewards is being processed, while approximately $1,477 in taxes is accumulating.

According to the project’s published mechanism, SWOLF transfers incur a 1% tax that funds holder distributions, primarily paid in STRK. In certain circumstances, when the platform holds a large share of SWOLF’s supply, rewards may instead be paid directly in SWOLF. Another approximately 2.5% of the tax is allocated to network and operating costs. For traders who want to hold SWOLF while accumulating STRK, this mechanism provides an additional incentive to hold.

However, the dollar value displayed on the reward dashboard does not equal holders’ realized net profits. The valuation of SWOLF rewards fluctuates with the token’s price and liquidity. Whether recipients sell their rewards or reinvest them in SWOLF also affects the final outcome. Transfer taxes add trading costs, which may become more noticeable when market activity slows.

The website also shows that SWOLF is included in the ecosystem flywheel rankings, with approximately $3.76 in cumulative buybacks and burns and three recorded buybacks. This shows that the mechanism has seen some activity, but the amount remains very small relative to overall trading volume. It is not enough to conclude that buybacks are providing meaningful buying pressure. The website also explicitly states that inclusion in the flywheel rankings does not guarantee future buybacks.

Therefore, I believe the market is betting on three things: first, whether Starknet’s new strategic narrative can continue attracting capital; second, whether SWOLF can become a recognizable memecoin representing the ecosystem; and third, whether its holder reward mechanism can turn short-term trading activity into more sustained demand to hold the token.

Looking at future catalysts, the first thing to watch is whether Starknet’s independent L1 plan receives a clearer technical roadmap, governance updates, and responses from the developer ecosystem. If this narrative continues gaining traction, STRK could remain in the spotlight, giving SWOLF an opportunity to benefit from spillover attention toward related assets. Second, SWOLF needs to build stronger community consensus, with more users actively embracing the wolf identity, participating in community activities, and spreading the narrative rather than appearing only when the price rises. Finally, the reward mechanism needs to demonstrate that it can remain attractive even when trading volume declines, while its distribution, buyback, and burn figures continue to be verifiable.

The main risks are SWOLF’s heavy dependence on STRK’s market momentum and its own trading activity. If the broader narrative cools, attention toward related assets could fade quickly. The large amount of SWOLF distributed as rewards could also turn into potential selling pressure.

My view is that SWOLF is a high-risk memecoin opportunity combining ecosystem connections, favorable timing, and observable reward data. What matters is not whether it can continue rising on the strength of the “Starknet wolf” label alone, but whether Starknet’s new narrative can endure, whether SWOLF can build an independent community, and whether its reward mechanism can continue generating genuine demand after market conditions cool.

If STRK remains strong while SWOLF’s holder and reward data continue improving, the rally could have room to continue. Conversely, if STRK loses momentum, SWOLF breaks below support, and rewards become a source of selling pressure, this rally may prove to have been driven primarily by short-term attention and liquidity rather than a sustainable revaluation of its ecosystem relevance.

text:
When I was leaving Singapore, something  happened that I think perfectly defines what Asia is.

We were leaving, it was 1 AM at Changi Airport, and I hadn’t slept all day (I always do this before taking a long flight)

We were checking in at the self-service machines, and I left my phone there.

I literally spent the next 20 minutes starting to sort out my luggage and going through the whole process.

Suddenly someone taps me on the shoulder from behind, and it’s a young guy asking me if that phone is mine.

You should’ve seen my face, I hadn’t noticed absolutely anything, I had even left my phone unlocked while doing the check-in.

I gave him a handshake followed by a hug because I was euphoric.

I don’t know where the young man was from, maybe judging by his accent he could’ve been from India, but what an amazing gesture from him.

There were so many people around, my phone was unlocked, and I wasn’t even aware that it was missing yet.

Believe me, if this had happened to me at any airport in Europe, I’m absolutely sure I would’ve had to say goodbye to my phone.

We have so much to learn from the kindness of people in Asia.

Seriously, what a beautiful gesture that really made me think.

text:
Assorted things I've been mulling over regarding agents in the economy:

• Companies are in some sense the original superintelligence. It's often the case that they can use their amortized cognitive surplus to advance their interests against those of certain consumers: relative to the optimization capacity of companies, consumers can be inattentive, underinformed, irrational, etc. (Think, say, of some of the classic insurance upsells at the end of a booking process, which is typically priced substantially above what a regular policy would cost.) Herbert Simon introduced the idea of bounded rationality, and firms often end up benefiting from it. Thanks to personal agents, we will probably get somewhat more rational in how we engage with companies.

• How exactly will outcomes change? Well, certain kinds of price discrimination will work less well (how do coupons work if every agent hunts fastidiously for them?), and certain kinds of customer cross-subsidy will change (today, people who forget to cancel subscriptions subsidize those who don't). Taken across the economy as a whole, I'm not sure what the incidence of all of this will be.

• In corporate strategy, people have long debated the relative importance of distribution and product quality. Perhaps you've made something better, but does anyone know about it? Won't people just continue to buy the ACME Corp Mousetraps? Personal agents will, I think, act as a kind of structural subsidy for product quality. How would markets look different if individuals always spent at least 10 hours researching their purchases? On the margin, focusing on making a product better is, I think, going to become a more effective strategy for companies. This is good!

• It true, a corollary is that information about product quality will become more important and impactful. Today, most people have very limited ability to aggregate and integrate such data, but agents will have insatiable thirst for such signals. (It's often said that data is becoming more valuable because it helps in the training of models. That's obviously true, but I think there's a secondary way in which it's more valuable simply as a complement to cheaper intelligence.)

• A big question is whether agents will increase superstar effects (rational agents all settle on the same product) or increase dispersion (because everyone has slightly different tastes and preferences, which agents are good at eliciting, finally overcoming the artificial clustering we've been subjected to).

• Many internet companies have monetized demand routing, which is in turn often predicated on short attention spans. "I'll click on the first thing I see." This has led to some amount of inefficiency, as companies try to propitiate capricious ranking algorithms and incur various placement fees. It's not all deadweight loss (willingness to pay is itself a kind of signal, which is valuable to buyers), but it's not great. How will the nature and value of this routing change in a world of personal agents? I don't know the answer, but I think that the effects might be pretty big.

• Much of what I'm writing hinges on the assumption that personal agents will be on the consumer's side. I suspect that that will be the winning strategy, but whether it's true, and what it means to be true, involves a lot of other questions.

Taken as a whole, the market is a massively parallelized, decentralized, and highly imperfect value attribution machine, and, taking stock of all of the effects, it seems to me that the quality point may well be the biggest: that agents will change the nature of the backpropagation such that the rewards for better products increase. Maybe this is too optimistic, but I suspect (and hope) that companies that make things that they're proud of will feel that the universe is a little more partisan in their favor.

text:
隨手記一下這次新加坡 TOKEN2049 的一些 takeaways：

1/ VC 不是沒錢，是錢開始往別的地方去了
這次跟幾家聊下來, 錢都還在, 但頭部幾家已經把重心挪到非 crypto 的項目 

2/ VC 現在最愛 infra
邏輯其實很簡單: 區塊鏈本質是技術, 技術本來就不應該很有趣

crypto 應該要很無聊，而且就該一直無聊下去

3/ @Polymarket 的空投內幕
參加了 polymarket private dinner 聽到的版本是: 中途插了 ICE 那筆投資, 整個空投計畫被迫延後, 重新思考

目前還是有在考慮, 最快明年, 但已經不是他們的首要考量了... 還在嚕的朋友得掂量一下

4/ 交易所全部都在轉型
方向很一致：美股、傳統金融, 把 TradFi 那套搬上鏈, 再加一點創新, 現在交易所都在趕著拿牌照上資產

listing 相關的部門可能會面臨大裁員, 畢竟現在已經沒有那麼多 crypto native 項目可以上了

5/ 今年遇到的團隊, 還活著的基本都轉型了
不是做 RWA、AI，就是做交易相關的 crypto
機會還在, 但幾乎都在往美國、往傳統市場靠 

除非你有很硬的場景，比如非洲的支付、東南亞的美股購買等等現在的項目得要有很強的應用場景以及現金流

6/ 交易所未來的對手是傳統金融的交易所
這是幣圈少數還贏、而且贏很多的地方: accessibility 跟 UI/UX

傳統金融的 app 大部分都太難用了

accessibility 講白一點, 就是在鏈上可以買到其他國家的股票, 現在在 @Bitget_zh @bitget 已經可以買到日股

台股最近也非常強 imagine 台股、日股、韓股全部都在鏈上, 這是個很大的機會 (不過合規也是個大問題)

@alloco_fi 最近在做的事情也正在風口上: 準備推 onchain ETF 跟 pre-IPO

pre-IPO 水很深, 但有機會 
onchain ETF 的優勢在於上鏈之後成本可以壓到幾乎零

這次跟不少傳統金融的高管以及行業裡的大佬聊過, 大家都覺得這個方向是對的, 大家可以期待一下

7/ AI 會比我們想的來得更快
這個都講爛了但我覺得大部分人還沒意識到多快, 現在做產品的時候，真的要開始考慮 agent first

以後用你產品的, 可能不是人

8/ Crypto 本來就該是個無聊的產業
它就是金融系統的一部分, finance 2.0 or whatever 總之就是一個大體系的一個小部分, 接受這件事之後, 反而比較看得清楚下一步要往哪走

幣圈這輪的變動很大, 這次 token 除了 @RaveDAO 基本上沒有超過 12點的活動, 你要說在走下坡好像也不大對, 畢竟是有pmf的 

只是這個pmf比我們前幾輪想像要小太多了…

以上是這次新加坡的觀後感, 各位老闆這次有什麼心得?

text:
Loss farming has already put early minters well ahead. Two things drove it: 1) PAPER supply was small at the start, and 2) large realized losses flowed to those first stakers.

However, as aggressive loss farming gives way to delta-neutral farming, protocol revenue (traders’ net losses) falls, and so does the effective price of minting PAPER relative to a real loss.

To illustrate, since PAPER is minted on losses (about 37 PAPER per $1 at today’s rate):

1. Pure loss farming: a $200K loss mints about 7.2M PAPER, and about $198K goes to stakers or tops up the pool.
2. Delta-neutral farming: the $200K lost on one leg mints the same 7.2M PAPER, but the winning leg takes most of it back, so the protocol keeps only about $27K.

That’s why, while minting PAPER should now cost about 2.7x what it did at launch, what stakers actually receive for each new PAPER has fallen, to about $2 per 1,000 new PAPER since the rush from nearly $5 during it. 

Adjusted for inflation, each staked PAPER now earns about 98% less per hour than during the rush. The planned increase in the pool cap from $5M to $10M will cut staker payouts further.

This is not to say staked PAPER won’t keep earning decent yields, but the extremely fast paybacks are over, and with them the reason to rush in and farm PAPER through pure losses. Anything you do now should be purely delta neutral, ideally on lowish leverage so you can close on bigger moves and avoid the insane haircuts.
author: shaundadevens
quoted_text:
Final thing before it’s time to get started: the report mostly assumes normal trading, not people losing on purpose.

A loss rush pays PAPER holders far more, since almost every dollar lost reaches stakers instead of going back to winners, so even pure loss farming could be profitable if you expect one.

Still, hedging will always give you higher return (it will just make it harder to put on size).

quoted_text:
我分析下来大概有几个原因：

1. 有些用户下载到假钱包，特别是中文区用户。因为在国内的浏览器搜索币圈的主流交易所和钱包，排前五的一直都是投了广告的假官网，前几年特别猖狂，最近2年百度和360有所好转，把TP的正版官网默认放在第一了，但是仍然需要翻墙才能打开。这些原因都增加了中文区用户下载到正版app的门槛。

2. 下载到正版app的用户也有很多私钥/助记词保存不当的操作，比如用手机截图保存私钥，使用微信的收藏夹、支付宝的钢铁匣等第三方保存，甚至还有人通过聊天软件发送私钥或者助记词。还有熟人作案，用户找不到被盗原因。这些被错误的归因为TP钱包本身有问题。

其实钱包被盗是概率问题，只有用户规模大的钱包才会导致被盗的绝对数高。比如之前大家在推特传某钱包很安全，那是因为那是并没有多少用户，后来用户规模上来后，这个钱包在推特上也开始大量出现被盗的案例。

3. 以上原因，让一些不明情况的用户误传，导致对TP的一些误解。很多用户根本没有使用过TP就黑。

TP钱包成立于2018年，8年多时间，从来没有出现过任何一起由于自己技术问题造成的用户资产被盗的情况。这些年我们也和各国各地的执法机构一起持续打击假钱包团队，相比前几年也取得了显著的成绩。

Raw thoughts on TOKEN2049 Singapore after attending for the third consecutive year.

- The worst weather by far.

- The main event itself was disappointing. 

I expected more. It’s only useful if you want merch or you’re interested in a specific panel or booth.

- can say the same about Sui Basecamp.

- Frontier Traders takes the crown as the most interesting and fun event.

- Really great people, I didn’t have a single bad experience or interaction.

- Many “high-profile” people turned out to be incredibly kind.

- Very pleasantly surprised by people who trade memecoins. 

Normally you’d think they’re assholes based on how they act here, but my experience was good.

- The best side event was @MetaMask 

Great people, great conversations, incredible food, and I loved the esoteric theme.

- Best merch goes to @Phantom.

- Wasting time in a crowded, noisy venue isn’t worth it unless you want to party.

- Incredible to spend time with friends from all over the world.

- A massive presence from traditional finance.

- There will be surprises with social trading over the coming months, It will be the narrative of this cycle.

- Web3 gaming is dead.

quoted_text:
Here’s essentially the expansion board broken down. It’s got two PCIE switches inside, meaning that you only need a singular x16 slot to power 8 GPUs (or two). 

Let’s talk about how it works. 

First, the main 8 GPUs slots

You have two methods of setup here:
- Direct connect via two PCIE x16 -> 4x x8 MCIO
- Cascade via a single PCIE x16 -> 2x x8 MCIO

The difference here is how much of your GPU usage do you want heading back to your CPU vs keeping everyone around one dimension for faster GPU -> GPU communication. 

A quick way to think about it: model fits on 8 GPUs? Cascade. CPU offload? Probably direct connect. 

But what IS cascade?

Let’s look back at the diagram. 

Direct connect says that we’re going to plug in two slots worth of x8 connectors into both 0-7 and 8-15 slots (two halves of our PCIE x16) into the separate halves. This then populates the switch in such a way that we can support 8 GPUs, each on separate 4-GPU P2P groupings. 

The nice part here is because the PCIE switches live in this board, you can take four additional MCIO cables and go from the output downlink into any one of the direct connect interfaces and add an additional GPU. 

BUT, if you want the two groups of 4 GPUs to interact, they’ll get tunneled through a single x16 slot worth of transfer, and have to go through the CPU. Not a fun bottleneck when dealing with 64 lanes worth of GPUs on either side. 

The alternative is what we call “cascade.” 

If we don’t want to worry about the CPU side (e.g. model inference), we can instead only hook up one PCIE slot as the input, then take the downlink from SW1 and use it as the INPUT to SW2. 

It’s still the bandwidth of a singular PCIE5 x16 slot, but you avoid going through the CPU which saves you some cycles. 

For the full 12 GPUs, you would need 3-4 full x16 slots on your motherboard. With the direct connect slots running through the host CPU still (since they are direct connect), if you’re not doing cascading. 

Or translation: 
- Non-DC: slot 1 and slot 12 are powered through additional retimers and MCIO at x16 and don’t add a slot, it’s just moving your existing PCIE slots somewhere else. Then you power slots 2 and 11 through the “jump” mentioned earlier
- DC: slot 1, 12, and then 2 or 11 are powered through a retimer, and then the other (between 2 and 11) are powered through the “jump”

Now let’s get into how I plan to use this. 

I have 9 GPUs in total (8 6000’s and a 6000 ADA), so I’ll be doing the Cascade, then using the SW2 output to power a 9th PCIE slot similar to the non-Cascade version that could power 10. 

What I don’t know yet is which is better: TP4/PP2, or TP8 over the two P2P groups, but I expect that would be the difference of batching. I’ll probably accept some slowness and do TP8. I can’t predict how much slower that will be, so when it comes in I’ll do these full benchmarks in many different combinations. 

What I want you to gather from this is these boards have internal PCIE switches, to help avoid needing to go through the CPU to have your GPUs interact, and bring you a larger lane budget than your CPU would allow.

The Copernican Model

Over the last few months, I’ve been studying the crypto models that seem to be discussed on a "fundamentals" basis: HYPE/Aave/Venice/etc, following the users/ revenue/relationship between a useful product and its token - all to create a sort of "value accural ontology." This is a case study from that research.

The reason was more selfish: I wanted to understand which models work when your business has to interact with the "real world," namely for how we want to take  @usdai_official for the most alignemnt

As a founder, I’ve had doors literally shut on my face when we started because we’re “crypto” (literally left in the waiting room like a tv show). I still believe tokenization is one of the most important technologies we have today. But the institutions we need to work with often want a equity counterparty, a board, and a contract. You just wont get around this for the next 10 years (no a cayman foundation doesnt work)

That experience has made me increasingly interested in the role of an equity surrogate: an independent operating business that connects a network to the world outside it.. but frankly there werent many clean examples out there without value destruction. 

The case I keep returning to is @tradexyz and Hyperliquid.. and im not really sure they even know how symbiotic of a relationship they created. They technically SHOULD be the same team.. but they are divided across the river due to regulatory issues, while being symbiotic

Consider the S&P 500 agreement, they licensed the benchmark to tradexyz for a perpetual market: the institutional relationship sits with the company, but the product runs on the network.

tradexyz can negotiate licenses, develop products, operate markets, and build distribution. Hyperliquid provides shared execution and settlement infrastructure. 

And if theres a company that ever wants "exposure" to the Hyperliquid business, but they just cant buy a "token" (and believe me, it's super super hard to get a traditional enterprise to buy a token, it doesnt fucking matter if you have an ETF, you literally have to convince a boomer board to do it and get the infrastructure set up to do it). Instaed, they could just invest in this equity, as it is not burning the HYPE it buys, but is increasing its share of it. so instead of buyback-n-burn, its closer to commit-n-compound.  

I’ve started thinking about this as a value-accrual architecture, with two different forms of capital (terms best described by a16z crypto's post in 2025):

Network asset: scarcity at the core.

- Its supply discipline can become more credible, its economics more programmatic, and its operation less dependent on any single company. 
- It coordinates shared infrastructure and connects activity across many businesses to a common asset.
- That is what I mean by a progressively hardening asset. The scarcity and independence have to be earned through the design of the system.
- Not capital intensive, as it must be smart contract based.
- Can often place be the seat of the "decentralized security" - as there is no central underwriter. If HYPE was a company.. itd be regulated out of the wazoo.

Enterprise equity: elasticity at the edge.

- A company can issue shares, raise capital, hire people, acquire licenses, and build products. 
- Its capital structure can expand with the work required to bring the network into the real world.
- New shares dilute ownership percentages, but productive investment can increase value per share. 
- That ability to finance expansion is why I think of equity as elastic
- This is the part where its OK to be regulated, because most of the regulational burden is held by HYPE, theyre just asset issuers.

These different traits are the reason to combine them.

An enterprise can raise the capital to grow while the network maintains its own supply discipline. The connection is the activity that expansion creates, and the mechanisms that route value from that activity back to the network.

Hyperliquid makes part of that relationship explicit. Trading generates fees for the deployer and the protocol. The Assistance Fund (insurance) automatically converts its allocated fees into HYPE, which the documentation specifies is burned. Hyperliquid fee mechanics

The broader strategy I take from this is Commit & Compound that is conducted around the equity enterprise. It's effectively what a DAT 2.0 would do: create a business first, then max-bid HYPE with that entity, then get new investors to invest in the convexity of HYPE^2.

Build a useful business around the network. Commit capital to its asset. Retain exposure to the infrastructure your business helps make more valuable.

For a company that accumulates and holds the network asset, growing enterprise value and participating in network value become connected opportunities. There is a business to capitalize and a shared ecosystem in which to hold an economic stake.

That is why I find the assumption that every successful application eventually needs its own token less compelling. Building a valuable company around an existing network asset is a meaningful strategy in its own right.

Notice how much kinetic language I’m using: commitment, circulation, gravity

I think network assets and enterprise assets represent different forms of gravity

HYPE is the sun: the network asset at the center

tradexyz equity is a planet: an enterprise building its business around that network

Its real-world integrations are moons: the licenses, institutional relationships, and distribution channels that gather around the enterprise and extend its reach

Enterprise value forms around network value. Real-world relationships form around enterprise value. Their activity feeds back into the shared system.

Personally, I think the greatest value can ultimately accrue at the network level. But that belief has to be substantiated by the businesses being built around it: real users, useful products, liquidity, and recurring economic activity.

A token doesn’t acquire gravity simply because we call it a network asset.

This is the distinction I found useful in a16z’s writing: can the network function and accrue value independently of the original company? Can other businesses build on it and contribute to its economics? 

The company can become a great business. The network can become the foundation for many great businesses.

Scarcity at the core. Productive expansion around it.

I’ve learned a lot from this Commit & Compound structure, with a Copernican asset at the center.

It has changed how I’m thinking about USDAI and CHIP. More on that in the next post

text:
USDC existing across dozens of blockchains is a good example of how crypto adoption is evolving.
But deploying an asset across more networks doesn't automatically make those networks work together.
Each chain maintains its own state, transaction history, and ownership records. For developers building applications across ecosystems, that creates additional complexity around coordination and reconciliation.

This becomes even more important as stablecoins are used in payments, automated workflows, and applications that operate across multiple environments.
@WireNetwork approaches this problem through its Universal Transaction Layer (UTL), designed to coordinate transactions and ownership while assets remain on their native chains.

The goal isn't to make every blockchain identical.
It's to make working across different ecosystems less complicated.
Distribution got assets everywhere. Coordination is the next challenge.

quoted_text:
USDC now lives across 38 blockchains.

Stablecoins can exist across dozens of networks.

In fact, the more environments an asset reaches, the more obvious the coordination problem becomes.

Where does the asset live?
Which address controls it?
How does ownership change?
How does an application interact with it across environments?

Distribution is only half the problem.

Coordination is the other half.

text:
Security remains our top priority for preserving trust in the XRP Ledger (XRPL). Sharing a few thoughts following yesterday's disclosure of the critical payments engine vulnerability reported by Veria AI.

First, this was a serious vulnerability, and we don't take that lightly. The bug had existed in the codebase for over a decade and could have allowed XRP to be created beyond its fixed supply. Fortunately, it was discovered through our bug bounty program before it could ever be exploited.

Second, our response was fast and coordinated. The team developed and thoroughly tested a fix, worked closely with validators to rapidly upgrade the network, and secured the ledger before public disclosure. I'm proud of how everyone came together to address the vulnerability and protect the XRPL network.

But there's a much bigger lesson here.

AI is fundamentally changing how quickly vulnerabilities can be discovered. We have to move even faster than before, especially with a codebase that's been around for over a decade.

This means we're doubling down in a few important areas:

* Proactive security: Strengthening our bug bounty programs, expanding AI-assisted vulnerability discovery/adversarial testing, and continuously improving testing across releases. This discovery reinforces why these investments matter.
* Addressing legacy tech debt: Working with our internal red team, external security researchers, and the XRPL Foundation to revisit longstanding assumptions in critical areas like payments engine, consensus, and P2P networking, guided by an updated threat model.
* Accelerating formal verification of critical areas: Continuing our work with CommonPrefix and the XRPL Foundation to apply formal verification to critical parts of the protocol, with the goal of uncovering deeper issues that other approaches could easily miss. We will build on the learnings from formal verification of the Lending Protocol and Single Asset Vault.
* Systemic hardening: Moving beyond individual bug fixes to identifying latent risks in older parts of the XRPL codebase and eliminating entire classes of vulnerabilities.

Our goal isn't simply to find more bugs. It's to systematically address the underlying risks and make the XRPL harder to exploit. As the XRPL's role in global financial infrastructure grows, so does our responsibility to protect it.

Security is never finished. We'll keep investing and improving alongside the broader XRPL community.

Full disclosure for the 3.4.1 release: https://t.co/7DshPd5pc2

Monetary Policy Update: Charter Stimulus and Branch Reductions

Standard has been incredibly efficient at bringing tokens back into the protocol. Burns are far outpacing issuance and nearly $1M has been deployed into buybacks and ETH-side liquidity.

With the upcoming launchpad and liquidity pools, Standard continues to build toward its larger vision.

While market conditions and activity on Robinhood Chain are outside the protocol's control, issuance appears to be heading toward another cut to 0.2×, the floor. This is the mechanism working as intended, tightening emissions when market activity slows.

However, the protocol's efficiency has allowed it to accumulate a significant surplus of STANDARD through POL fees, putting it in a unique position to support long-term Charter holders despite broader market conditions.

As part of this issuance cut, the number of branches available per auction will be reduced to 25, further slowing the growth of future issuance.

To reward that long-term commitment, the protocol will also distribute a portion of its accumulated surplus as a one time bonus to eligible existing branches, bringing their payout to the equivalent of approximately 0.7× issuance for that distribution.

Eligibility will be limited to Charters that have purchased at least one branch through open-market auctions, demonstrating long-term commitment to the protocol. Claim is live on the site's announcements.

The issuance multiplier will still fall to 0.2× and every token distributed will come from what the protocol has already earned.

群友问，之前safe出过那么大问题，还可以用safe吗？

这个需要两方面看

首先，safe合约代码安全性很高，目前为止没有公开的被黑事件，原因是核心代码逻辑简单和区块链无法篡改的特性，除非获得safe的多签，否则即使神仙也是无法修改。

其次，safe的前端有被攻击的例子，参考bybit被盗十几亿美金，原因就是前端被修改，让多签者以为是普通的交易，实际签的是把钱包底层合约替换成攻击者恶意合约的交易。

如果使用safe，注意以下几点

- 把官网加入收藏夹，不要相信搜索和其他人链接
- 尽量不要盲签，最好能在硬件钱包屏幕上看清楚资金金额和收款方（尽量只做转账操作，不要做其他defi交互）
- 找第三方工具做模拟交易看运行结果
- 自己电脑不要被感染

另外有一点，safe前端被定向攻击的例子是极少的，上次只针对bybit，如果散户资金不大的话，无法覆盖定向攻击成本

总之， 3个不同厂商不同私钥的硬件钱包+safe 2/3多签，对于散户目前看是安全级别很高的措施

这期《未来12个月，普通投资人要关注的科技资产信号》的核心是：AI与比特币仍有机会，但看对方向只是第一步，买入价格、时机、仓位和承受回撤的能力，才决定最终收益。 以下为嘉宾观点整理：

AI长期趋势仍被看好，短期政策冲击可能提供买点。 嘉宾认为，美国中期选举中的限制AI议题，可能打击市场情绪、引发相关资产回调，却未必改变产业长期发展。但对时间点存在分歧：有人等待选举后的机会，Jason则认为市场会提前交易预期，调整可能在选举过程中完成。

AI产业链中，半导体的受益逻辑相对清晰。 开源与闭源模型谁最终获胜、应用层哪家公司跑出来，都尚不确定；但各方都需要芯片、CPU、存储和光通信。因此，嘉宾更倾向通过半导体指数参与整体建设周期，同时认为当前交易拥挤，需要关注买入价格。

AI的新增长点是开箱即用的“数字员工”。 AI正在从需要用户折腾的工具，变成能持续执行任务的助手，例如管理日程、收集新闻、处理订单和旅行计划。关键突破既包括操作软件的能力，也包括易用性与信任：用户愿意授予权限，AI才能承担更多实际工作。商业化能否兑现，还需观察收入表现。

Jason更偏向比特币，强调在悲观时期寻找机会。 他认为，比特币具备长期前景，而录制时市场情绪尚不乐观，风险收益比更有吸引力。不过，长期看好并不意味着短期不会继续跟随市场下跌。

判断价格，要区分新闻刺激与持续的供需变化。 Jason以石油为例：停战等新闻可能制造短期涨跌，而供应受限、库存下降和补库存需求，才可能持续影响价格。研究应关注事件是否真正改变供给与需求。

研究正确，不等于交易赚钱。 Jason分享了看多农产品，却在上涨前卖出的经历：方向判断正确，仍可能因时机和仓位失误而亏损。仓位过大会让人扛不住波动；认知不足，即便买入也可能拿不住。配置应匹配自己的资金、心理和身体承受能力。

text:
My Thoughts on $CLAUDIA, $JEANPHIL, and AI-Native Virtual IP

I believe AI-native virtual IP is emerging as a new industry, although it has not yet become a clearly defined, mature industry with established business models. More accurately, it is an emerging sector at the intersection of AI technology, entertainment IP, virtual idols, digital humans, short-form video, and fan economics.

The key distinction is whether AI is simply a tool used to create IP, or the underlying production model through which that IP is created and operated from the very beginning.

Traditional virtual IP is nothing new. Virtual idols, anime characters, game characters, and virtual influencers have existed for years. The real change is that AI is significantly lowering the cost of character creation, music production, video generation, and ongoing operations, while giving characters new opportunities to interact continuously with their audiences. Deloitte, a media and entertainment industry research firm, has also identified the integration of generative AI into everyday creative workflows and the rise of AI musicians and virtual influencers as trends worth watching.

So why do I believe this is becoming a new sector?

There are three developments worth paying attention to.

1. Character production is shifting from project-based creation to continuous operation.

In the past, building a virtual character typically required teams specializing in modeling, animation, screenwriting, voice acting, and operations. AI is lowering the costs across these areas, giving individual creators the opportunity to continuously produce music, videos, stories, and social media content around the same character.

In 2026, Japan's Dentsu launched CHARAMO, an AI-driven IP growth platform covering character development, social media content, character chat, podcasts, and merchandise. This shows that the industry is beginning to explore how AI can be used to operate characters continuously, rather than simply generate individual pieces of content.

2. Characters have the potential to evolve from content people watch into interactive digital personalities.

The difference between traditional virtual IP and AI-native virtual IP is becoming increasingly clear.

Traditional virtual IP: Characters are designed by teams and reach fans through animation, comics, games, performances, and other forms of content. Interaction and content updates generally depend on the production team.

AI-native virtual IP: Characters can continuously generate different forms of content and maintain relationships with users through conversations, personalized responses, and community interactions. They have the potential to evolve from protagonists in individual pieces of content into digital personalities that can be operated over the long term.

There are already concrete commercial experiments in this direction. For example, in 2026, WEBTOON partnered with Genies, with plans to turn comic characters into interactive digital avatars, exploring new fan experiences and monetization opportunities for creators.

3. The barriers to producing and operating IP may both decline.

In the past, whether a character could become a commercially valuable IP depended heavily on the production resources behind it. AI gives more creators the opportunity to develop characters, but it also means that the supply of content will grow rapidly.

Ultimately, the competitive advantage may shift from who can produce content to who can create characters that people remember and continuously build their influence over time.

AI lowers the barrier to producing characters, not the barrier to building a successful IP.

Applying this idea to projects such as CLAUDIA and JEANPHIL, we can view them as early experiments in this emerging sector. Creators use AI to produce content continuously, build attention around a consistent character, and then attempt to develop that character into an independent entertainment IP.

However, two layers need to be distinguished:

At the IP level: Can the character develop a stable audience, a coherent body of content, and cultural influence?
At the token level: Can that influence generate sustained demand for the token and a clear mechanism for value capture?

Success at the first level does not guarantee success at the second. A character can become a popular virtual IP while its associated memecoin still lacks a sustainable economic mechanism.

My conclusion is that AI-native virtual IP is an emerging industry worth paying attention to. But the long-term opportunity is not about how many videos AI can generate. It is about whether AI enables more people to create virtual characters that attract sustained attention, independently expand their own content worlds, and eventually become commercially valuable IPs—and whether the associated tokens can capture some of that value.

Let's talk about $JEANPHIL and $CLAUDIA, and why I'm bullish on the AI Influencer + short-form video narrative.

First, the broader sector.

I believe AI Influencers combined with short-form video distribution could become one of the narratives worth watching in the next Meme market cycle.

The underlying logic is simple: AI is turning character creation from a high-cost, low-frequency process into a low-cost, scalable content business that can be operated continuously. In the past, building an influencer required appearance, performance, filming, editing, and long-term management. Now, creators can use AI to design characters, develop personalities, produce short videos, and even operate multiple virtual personas simultaneously.

But what really matters isn't how many characters AI can generate. It's whether those characters can consistently produce content that people want to watch, discuss, and follow.

Short-form video drives distribution, characters accumulate attention, and Memes can become a speculative vehicle for that attention in the crypto market. An AI character can build a distinctive persona through continuous video releases, participate in trending topics, create new memes, and interact with other characters, gradually evolving from a single viral clip into a recognizable IP.

Compared with traditional Memes that rely on an isolated event or a single image, these characters theoretically have the ability to continuously generate new material for distribution. If a character develops a stable audience and cultural recognition, it no longer has to rely entirely on a single viral moment to maintain attention.

If this model gains traction in the crypto market, speculation may shift beyond the next viral image toward AI characters that have already attracted genuine attention on platforms like TikTok and Instagram, can consistently produce content, and have the potential to channel that external attention on-chain.

This is why I've chosen to take a deeper look at JEANPHIL and CLAUDIA. They represent two different paths within this emerging narrative.

JEANPHIL: External traction that has already emerged.

Jean Phil is an AI-generated French male character. His blond bowl cut, curled mustache, brown houndstooth suit, and signature street-style boxing moves create a recognizable visual identity that is easy to imitate.

The character has attracted significant attention on TikTok and Instagram, generating imitations and derivative content. This demonstrates how an AI character with a distinctive persona and a simple, replicable video format can quickly capture attention on mainstream social platforms.

The logic is straightforward: the character attracts external traffic, the content inspires imitations and remixes, and that attention may eventually flow into its on-chain token.

Compared with Memes that rely solely on narratives originating within crypto, JEANPHIL already has an external source of attention. What it needs to prove next is whether that momentum can persist and whether the character's popularity can translate into sustained token demand.

CLAUDIA: From AI creation toward long-term IP development.

CLAUDIA is more focused on long-term IP development. Around Claudia, anabology has been building Claudia Gallery and proposed creating an open version of Hatsune Miku for the AI era. Related initiatives also include AI character creation tools, Agent Skills, and Claudia Local.

The Influencer mode brings this vision closer to the AI Influencer model: by continuously producing videos, maintaining a consistent character identity, and experimenting with high-frequency publishing, it aims to gradually build its own audience.

The logic is that AI lowers content production costs, continuous video output helps establish character recognition, and the character gradually accumulates an audience before attempting to convert that external attention into IP influence and on-chain interest.

Compared with JEANPHIL, CLAUDIA has greater potential in the direction of a long-term AI creator ecosystem. The goal isn't simply to make a character go viral in the short term, but to explore how an AI character can continuously produce content, build an audience, and develop into an expandable, open IP.

However, this path has a longer chain of validation. Being able to produce videos consistently doesn't mean the content will necessarily gain traction. Having creation tools doesn't guarantee the ability to build a successful character. And an open-IP vision doesn't automatically mean the token can capture the resulting value.

Although both projects fall under the broader AI Influencer narrative, their trading theses are different.

JEANPHIL is more focused on existing external traction. The key question is whether that attention can persist and translate into token demand. CLAUDIA is more focused on AI creation capabilities and long-term IP development. The key question is whether it can consistently produce compelling content and build a genuine audience.

What I'm bullish on is the shared potential behind both approaches: AI characters could evolve beyond static images into dynamic IPs that continuously produce content, participate in trending topics, build social relationships, and generate new Memes.

Of course, a compelling sector narrative doesn't mean every related token will appreciate.

We need to distinguish three separate outcomes: an AI character gaining attention, an IP building lasting influence, and a token capturing value from that influence. A character can become popular without benefiting its token. A project can have impressive creation tools without producing viral content. Even if an IP continues to grow, attention may remain entirely off-chain if the token has no meaningful connection to its development.

Therefore, what I'm really looking for isn't the first token to announce that it uses AI, but projects that have demonstrated their ability to attract external attention, consistently produce distributable content, and establish a clear connection between that attention and their tokens.

AI is the production tool, short-form video is the distribution channel, character IP is the vehicle for attention, and the token represents a separate speculative market.

When these four elements become genuinely connected, AI Influencers could evolve from a trending concept into a new Meme narrative with sustained distribution potential.

In my view, the projects most likely to break out will need a distinctive character identity, consistent content distribution, a genuine external audience, and a mechanism for translating attention into token demand. That's why I'm bullish on this direction and have chosen to take a deeper look at JEANPHIL and CLAUDIA.

text:
如果你不是很懂的话，最好不要用硬件钱包。我跟你讲讲为什么：

1. 硬件钱包都很贵，供应链没有话语权
就一个小小的东西带个屏幕，好像就要卖 2000 多。它贵的原因其实很简单：产量小，自己又没有工厂，在供应链上根本没有话语权。只能找别人代工定做，订货量少，价格自然而然就上去了。

2. 安全性根本比不过苹果
你在安全上能投入多少钱？苹果在 iPhone 的安全上能投入多少钱？黑客面对的是你这么一家做硬件钱包的小公司，还是全球市值前五的苹果公司？这完全不是一个量级的。而且苹果还有漏洞赏金计划，找到漏洞是有奖金拿的。

你说苹果手机能不能破解？我相信能够破解，但除非你是超级恐怖分子那个级别的，估计摩萨德和CIA才愿意花大精力、大财力来破解你的手机。普通人哪怕牵扯到经济类犯罪或者杀人案，他们根本没兴趣、也没那个财力去费劲破解你的手机。谁会为了这点小案件，就是一个简单的杀人案或者经济类犯罪，去突破法律的底线来破解？不值得呀，也拿不到什么功劳。

最好用美国团队、美国公司的产品。我为什么推荐用 Coinbase 的钱包app呢？因为它在美国已经是上市公司了，以后真的出了什么问题，也好走诉讼程序。你钱要是很少，就几万美元，那无所谓的，随便放哪里都可以，没了就没了，反正不是送给庄家就是送给黑客了。

但你如果钱很多的话，就得考虑万一出了问题，至少能不能拿一半回来？那就要走诉讼程序了，对吧？

当然，谁要是选美国企业，美国至少还有全球执法能力，懂吧？你搞个注册实体在迪拜、新加坡的，没人理你的，谁理你？

你搞什么其他钱包团队之类的，整天弄得神神秘秘、跟地下党一样，连法律主体是什么你都不知道。然后他们去买一大堆 KOL 宣传自己钱包有多好，真要出了问题他们根本没办法解决，因为财力不够，你懂吧？是一个创业团队，创业团队什么意思呢？成功了，他们就是王；失败了，你就是那个代价，懂吧？

团队如果在美国的话，就像那个 FTX 一样，至少还能拿点钱回来；fcoin，你一毛钱都别想拿回来，就是这个道理啊。

我之前每次都买 20 个，然后混着用。当时我就担心里面会给我植入什么东西，怕里面给我加其他芯片进去，我还特地拆了两个出来看，都仔细研究过了

text:
Expression is the core energy of existence. Every expression carries information, a certain rhythm, and a cause and effect. It can bring either chaos or peace into material reality.

Every living being expresses itself through nature’s rhythm. But humans are increasingly losing that rhythm because of what we eat, breathe, drink, think, and consume through our screens.

The Taittiriya Upanishad says:

अन्नं ब्रह्मेति व्यजानात्।

Food is Brahman.

Our nourishment shapes our biology, our biology influences our thoughts, and our thoughts influence our expressions.

Now think about the Divine Mother.

The Devi Mahatmyam says:

या देवी सर्वभूतेषु शक्तिरूपेण संस्थिता।

The Goddess resides in all beings as Shakti.

Perhaps what we call creation, destruction, chaos, and order are different manifestations of that same energy.

Today, information flows through silicon, but its consequences unfold through carbon-based life. From a nondual perspective, both belong to the same Prakriti. There is no separation in the eyes of the Divine Mother.

And perhaps humanity is going through another season of transformation, where destruction and creation coexist.

But here’s the real meaning of Navratri for me.

If the Divine Mother exists in every being, worshipping her cannot end at the temple.

The food you waste, the nature you destroy, the people you hurt, the body you neglect, and the thoughts you feed yourself - all deserve your attention.

Because every expression has consequences.

Perhaps the purpose of Navratri is not to invite the Divine Mother into our homes for nine nights, but to realize that we have never spent a single moment outside her presence.

Worship her through your actions, not just rituals.

Jai Ma.

Monetary Policy Update: Charter Stimulus and Branch Reductions

Standard has been incredibly efficient at bringing tokens back into the protocol. Burns are far outpacing issuance and nearly $1M has been deployed into buybacks and ETH-side liquidity.

With the upcoming launchpad and liquidity pools, Standard continues to build toward its larger vision.

While market conditions and activity on Robinhood Chain are outside the protocol's control, issuance appears to be heading toward another cut to 0.2×, the floor. This is the mechanism working as intended, tightening emissions when market activity slows.

However, the protocol's efficiency has allowed it to accumulate a significant surplus of STANDARD through POL fees, putting it in a unique position to support long-term Charter holders despite broader market conditions.

As part of this issuance cut, the number of branches available per auction will be reduced to 25, further slowing the growth of future issuance.

To reward that long-term commitment, the protocol will also distribute a portion of its accumulated surplus as a one time bonus to eligible existing branches, bringing their payout to the equivalent of approximately 0.7× issuance for that distribution.

Eligibility will be limited to Charters that have purchased at least one branch through open-market auctions, demonstrating long-term commitment to the protocol. Claim is live on the site's announcements.

The issuance multiplier will still fall to 0.2× and every token distributed will come from what the protocol has already earned.

I have been long 3x on $AERO and positioned for the run into the upgrade (I think it will run somewhere around ~1.3, obv a NFA)

So far the trade has played out well. Will be a good trade for me if it hit my levels.

Also I'll be holding my spot bags still as it's my only main base exposure play). Saying this cuz once a tokenised stock gets issued, it needs liquidity every time someone buys, sells or rotates out. The issuer might get the listing but whoever owns that liquidity gets paid on every trade after. That's the thing @aeroxyz is going for across Base, RH and Arc, all feeding one revenue system.

➥ With Predictive Allocation, sAERO holders direct incentives to pools and earn the revenue those pools generate
➥ Allocations can shift every 48H at launch
➥ So every new stock or stablecoin market competes for allocators, not just traders
