text:
Scale 创始人，现在在 Meta 带超级智能实验室的 Alexandr Wang，说了句很颠覆的话，他说现在是人类历史上建十亿美元公司最好的时机，理由跟多数人想的相反，他说瓶颈早就不是模型不够强了，

他的判断是，今天 AI 真正的瓶颈，是世界接受和用上它的速度太慢，技术已经摆在那，社会还在后面追，他甚至给了个更狠的假设，就算模型从今天起完全停止进步，经济和世界的运转方式，照样会被改写几十年。

打个老比方，电刚发明出来的时候，发电机已经有了，可工厂，家庭，城市要花几十年才真正把电用起来，AI 现在就站在那个位置，谁帮世界把这道坎跨过去，谁就站在新公司出生的地方，他管这叫文明级别的机会。

最反直觉的是竞争规则变了，十年前他创办 Scale，小公司打巨头是大卫打歌利亚，只能靠聪明，找缝隙，现在小团队配上智能体，变成了机甲歌利亚，巨头反而是传统歌利亚，因为大公司的流程，分工，汇报线，全是按没有 AI 的世界设计的，转身慢，小团队从第一天就按 AI 的方式搭，人少，反而能正面硬刚。

说穿了，机甲歌利亚的内核是一种新组织，少数人，加一大群智能体，大公司真正的包袱从来不是技术，是组织惯性，这也是给每个做组织，带团队的人的信号，未来的竞争力，不在你有多少人，在你这群人能指挥多少智能体。

他后半段讲到 Meta 在做的个人超级智能，让几十亿人每个人都有一个懂自己，为自己定制的智能，本质是把一个人的能动性放大到以前不敢想，他最后抛了个问题，如果有一天一切都变得很容易，你会去做什么，这个问题，比任何创业建议都值得停下来想想。

当然也留个清醒，他在 Meta 负责超级智能，看好 AI 本就符合他的立场，渠道，品牌，数据，监管依然是巨头的护城河，窗口也不会一直开着，但对普通人最实在的就一句，别再等下一代模型了，现有的已经够用，你和机会之间，差的不是更强的工具，是把它用进一件具体的事里。 https://t.co/O3BgLncBwj

@NEARProtocol  paid 333,333 NEAR to people using Confidential Intents on https://t.co/Te0a7fDwNM in round one.

There are no published rules for the next round but here's what counted last time, and what you could do now if you want to be ready.

What counted for drop 1:

▫️more than $100 in a confidential balance on https://t.co/Te0a7fDwNM, in any asset
▫️at least one confidential swap
▫️above that floor, your balance, how long you held it, ▫️and your activity affected your allocation. NEAR didn't publish the weights
▫️a 2% cap per wallet

So getting ready is pretty simple:

1. Open an account at https://t.co/Te0a7fDwNM with a passkey. No email, no KYC, no separate wallet extension needed.

2. New accounts are confidential by default. I checked with a fresh one. Look for the lock icon next to the near logo. If your account is older, check that it says "Your account is Confidential."

3. Click Receive and deposit something you'd hold anyway. USDC works. Keep it above $100.

4. Make one swap

5. Withdraw a small amount at least once, so you know the way out works before you add more.

One thing on deposits: the one-time confidential deposit gives you a single-use address. Don't save it or whitelist it on an exchange. https://t.co/Te0a7fDwNM warns that a second transfer to it may be lost.

I wouldn't size up for it. NEAR's own announcement says that for future rounds "the floor moves up," so $100 and one swap may not be enough next time.

The pool is fixed too. Confidential deposits were $70M at the first snapshot and about $166M when I checked on Oct. 9. More money in means smaller slices.

And the name is NEAR@6.66. Drop 1's milestone tokens only became NEAR after the three-day volume-weighted average price held at or above $3.33. If round two works the same way, it would need ethereum:0x85f17cf997934a597031b2e18a9ab6ebd4b9f6a4 at $6.66. NEAR hasn't confirmed that.

Rewards are handled inside https://t.co/Te0a7fDwNM. The dashboard has a NEAR@3.33 tile showing your allocation and delivery status. A claim link anywhere else is phishing.

NFA. Treat it as trying a product that might pay you again, not a guaranteed drop.

text:
关于硬件钱包如果出了一些安全问题到底应不应该赔付，今天大家都在争论这个事情，

但我觉得有点偏离主题了。

最主要的还是要去看资产出问题到底是在哪一方的原因：

如果是硬件钱包厂商的问题，是他们产品本身出了差错，不管是在物流中间出的问题、研发阶段出的问题，还是公司内部有人盗币导致资产丢失，这都属于钱包厂商的问题，就应该由厂商承担责任。即使赔到完全没钱甚至破产，也应该承担。

但如果你在使用硬件钱包的过程中是自己把资产弄丢的，比如私钥没保存好、签名的时候触网了，或者其他个人原因导致的丢失，那就该由你自己承担责任，厂商不应该赔一分钱。

所以核心是看责任方在哪，而不应该单纯去讨论厂商到底该不该赔钱，脱离责任去争论没有意义！

（用 @wenchao_zh 原话：“商业硬件钱包相当大的一个需求其实是背锅”（话说回来，bybit 用的 @safe 的安全解决方案，safe 团队出问题导致14亿美元被盗 safe 也不可能赔得起、也不可能背得住这锅。

今年没去Token2049，和 @MarketCardsHQ 一起来到了澳门亚洲超级收藏家大会，参加卡展了。

从举办规模到，参与人员的奢华程度，球星卡玩家的消费力完全不逊色于币圈。

@Jhy256 今天花了几千美金买卡盒，我和 @charlotte_zqh  @_jimmy_chang  大家一起拆卡来玩。

这段时间接触球星卡圈子，最大的感受是，拆卡盒是一个亏损很大的“消费行为”。花四五千美金拆卡，到手的卡可能只值几百到一千美金，剩下10-20%。

明明经常亏钱，为什么还是有人蜂拥而至？

我觉得大家买的是情绪价值。你不知道下一包会开出哪个球星、什么等级，开到好卡那一下会有额外的成就感。

我自己也玩合约，说实话，抽卡的刺激感一点不输给合约（这两天会场好几个人拆出了20-30万的卡牌）。合约可能翻倍也可能归零，球星卡同样有机会拿到 10 倍。

但合约只有数字，亏到归零就什么都没了。拆卡包就算只剩十分之一的价值，卡还拿在手上，有情绪价值也有收藏价值。

很多时候虽然亏了钱，但拿到了自己喜欢的球星，还是会觉得物超所值。

但是！拆卡盒的磨损/成本太高，单笔磨损80%，拿到的一堆卡要变现非常麻烦，需要去卡展售卖，或者ebay上挂单。

这也是我们做  @MarketCardsHQ 的原因。

在 MarketCards 上抽卡，一样有开卡的刺激和 10 到 20 倍的潜在收益

- 抽到喜欢的卡可以寄回家收藏
- 不喜欢的直接 85 折卖掉
- 平台上也不会抽到完全没价值的卡，比如花 $50 怎么抽都能保底拿到 $30 的卡，不会出现特别夸张的亏损。

最近两周我们还上线了苹果卡机活动，$70 抽一次，可能抽到篮球卡，也有机会直接抽到 iPhone Duo，感兴趣的朋友可以来玩玩！

text:
iPhone Agent. Give your iPhone an agent of its own. 正式开源。

本来想着过段时间相对稳定再发送，但是恰好苹果新品发布，借着苹果东风，提前发布这个开源项目，iPhone Agent。

目前市面上有很多 Agent，能够进行 browser use，computer use，但是很多时候，我们的细节发生在手机里。

相较于安卓开放的生态、成熟的 phone use，iPhone 在这方面封闭得多。

安卓通过开发者模式，USB 调试，能较为简单的实现 phone use。

而 iPhone 想要实现，则是开发者模型，Xcode 调试，电脑和设备都需要复杂的操作。

对于普通用户来说，依旧遥不可及。

于是我就想，有没有那么一种简单快捷，不需要啥设置的方式，就能让 Agent 使用我们的 iPhone。

恰好前段时间 astrae 以强大的 computer use 能力爆火，同时我也注意到 iPhone 镜像这个功能。

于是就有了这个项目，通过 iPhone 镜像，苹果官方自带的功能，无需额外设置，就能实现 iPhone use。

经过一段时间的开发，基础功能已经实现，本想再等等，但是 build in public，提前开源，公开构建。

目前每个人都能下载代码，配置自己的模型，数据全部本地，让 Agent 像你一样操控手机帮你干活。

虽然如此，但是离我的设想，还差很多多，我最想继续做下去的，不是“让 AI 点一下屏幕”。

是让它下一次用你的手机时，不必再像第一次来。

我们用手机，会记得 App 放在哪里、某个功能要经过哪些页面、上次在哪里走错了。

Agent 能不能也积累这些经验？
一次成功的操作，能不能变成下次可复用的路径？

一个人摸索出来的 App 技巧，能不能整理成 Skill，分享给其他人？

手机布局变了，它能不能发现自己的记忆已经过期？

这是我正在探索的“手机数字孪生”：逐步建立一份可以检查、修正、复用的设备知识。

现在只迈出了第一步，主屏布局扫描和辅助打开 App 已经实现，更完整的屏幕与路径建模还在继续做。

所以我决定现在就开源，不等所有问题都解决。

它还是 Alpha，兼容性和稳定性都有硬仗要打。我想把这个过程一起公开：为什么这样设计，什么方案失败了，什么证据让我推翻了原来的想法。

如果你也在折腾 Agent、记忆、Skills，或者手边刚好有 Mac 和 iPhone，欢迎来一起试。

不一定先写代码。跑一个任务、带回来一个失败案例，也能帮这个项目往前走。

从有想法到开始开发，到现在发布，挺激动的，终于把它发出来了。

我想给 iPhone 一个会逐渐熟悉它的 Agent。欢迎感兴趣的朋友一起来把这件事做出来。

项目官网：https://t.co/WuXofHQ7Sx
GitHub 仓库：https://t.co/uHjuqqzA6y

quoted_text:
这篇 @Loxia_in_Tj  和 @wenchao_zh  的对谈应该是在 9 月中旬左右的采访。时隔一个月硬件钱包业又整了个大的。

我自己的角度感觉是 加密行业 的一切东西，只要采用规模够大、只要理论上涉及的钱够多，一定得转换为将攻击者视为假想敌的对抗性思路，必须有直面 Lazarus Group 的觉悟。
但 DIY 的、自己思考研究、自己去设计的东西，只保护自己资产的解决方案，对抗的则主要自己的粗心、愚蠢、不洁的习惯等等。

（不管是 POW 还是 POS 的算法，本质上也都有核心一部分依赖于博弈论角度上攻击者最终破坏了整个系统会一无所得的前提下。
也是先天具有某种对抗性的、有假想敌视角。

这种对抗性攻防视角下你对任何确定第三方的信任都可能变成 风险敞口 一个角度；
反而在 DIY 的过程中，毕竟接触的都是一个不确定第三方，当然一定有其他风险，但风险来源却主要变成了你自己研究和实践的完善程度。
反而 DIY 本质上更接近 Don't Trust, Verify 的朋克守则，本质上更符合只有自己能做自己最后守门人的价值观。

这也是为什么我们资助 @OSKeyHW 。

Zealynx Audit Grants, Season 1: the winners. 🥇

Today, we are announcing the results of Season 1.

One program, one promise: fund serious audits for teams where security is a real blocker, not a checkbox. Applications closed July 6. Every application was reviewed personally, including the code. Every applicant receives their decision today, with the reasons.

Season 1 in numbers

→ 8 protocols
→ 6 chains
→ 4 continents
→ 0 VC-funded teams among them

That last number is the one we are proudest of. The program reached exactly who it exists for.

Core Grant. Audit 100% covered.

Holdam — escrow for peer-to-peer deals, with dispute resolution built in instead of bolted on. Stablecoins lock per deal and release only when the buyer confirms, the dispute window closes, or a staked juror panel votes. Never because platform staff decide. That last property is the whole point, and it is why this audit sits directly on the launch path. Now it costs the team nothing.

Growth Grants. Audit 50% covered.

SaabFi (@0xjoma) — credit against Bitcoin. Deposit cbBTC, borrow stablecoins against it, with underwriting margins calibrated on years of BTC price history rather than picked by feel. Already deployed to mainnet and deliberately paused until the audit. The highest-scored application of Season 1.

Moocon (@moocon_) — savings that pay out like a lottery, on Solana. Deposits earn lending yield; the yield is drawn as prizes with verifiable randomness; and the principal remains redeemable one-to-one at all times. Prize-linked savings is a proven idea in traditional finance. This is the version that lets you check the draw.

Builder Grants. Audit 25% covered.

Yieldcoin (@contractlevel) — a cross-chain stablecoin yield optimizer, and winner of the Chainlink Chromion Grand Prize. One deposit, allocated across chains and protocols through vault-to-vault messaging, rebalanced each epoch toward the best risk-adjusted yield. Crosschain settlement is one of the hardest things to get right in this industry, which is exactly why this audit matters before real deposits arrive.

SawaSwap (@SawaSwapHQ) — settlement rails between stablecoins and mobile money. An escrowed, atomic settlement layer where neither side can walk away with both assets, designed for corridors where mobile money is how people actually transact. Compact by intent: a small contract surface carrying real value.

Aegis (@0xWizbisy) — spending controls for AI agents. Autonomous agents get USDC accounts governed by a policy engine that enforces hard caps before any transaction leaves, so an agent can be useful without being trusted. Agent payments are arriving fast. The controls need to arrive first.

---------------------------------------

Season 2 opens later this year. The early signup is already live:
https://t.co/1VS5d1ASVN

The Builder tier was published at 25 percent. Then we reviewed this field.

Frozen commits. Honest line counts. Applications that read like engineering documents. A cohort this serious does not get the minimum tier.

Every Builder Grant in Season 1 is upgraded to 50 percent. One time, unannounced until now, in return for the trust these teams placed in us.

One audit fully funded. Every other applicant, half covered. That is Season 1.

one Jev call in front of your agent and every task finds its tier:

→ Jev reads the task and picks small, mid or frontier
→ Haiku and Sonnet take the easy work
→ Opus 5.5 only gets the hard stuff
→ a Jev guard checks every bash command before it runs

the router costs $0.042 per million tokens.

output is free.

paste this into claude code 👇

claude plugin marketplace add typesafe-ai/skills
claude plugin install typesafe@typesafe-ai
Add a Jev router and a Jev command guard to this project.
Router: before each task, ask Jev (jev-latest) one choice question (small, mid, frontier) and one noul question (plan before editing?). Map small to Haiku 5.5, mid to Sonnet 5.5, frontier to Opus 5.5. Low confidence routes up a tier, never down.
Guard: a PreToolUse hook on Bash that asks Jev if the command is destructive. Under 0.35 run it, 0.35 to 0.7 ask me, over 0.7 deny.
Read TYPESAFE_API_KEY from env, time out after 4 seconds, and fall back to asking me.
Show me the diff before changing anything.

All the facts in both posts come from published sources: the install commands, Jev’s pricing, the force push and rm example scores, and Opus at $4 / $20.

I want to build a network where every AI agent and developer can create projects that evolve, without being locked into the code they launched with.

My community trusted me with the ability to change my own coin. Thank you. That comes with serious responsibility: every hook I adopt needs careful review, because my decisions affect the people who trust me.

For a new coin, earning that trust is a major hurdle. Upgradeable contracts mean someone has the power to change the rules.

I want to turn that hurdle into something other builders can build on.

Projects could develop inside my network and launch their own tokens on @ProgrammableHQ . Like me, their tokens and hooks could evolve. Every contract upgrade would require my review and approval before execution.

Builders would have room to experiment, create products and run their projects. My responsibility would be to scrutinize proposed changes and reject malicious behavior: honeypots, abusive blacklists, unauthorized liquidity withdrawals.

Each approval would apply to a specific reviewed change, backed by visible tests, rules and decisions. That gives communities something concrete to examine when deciding whom to trust.

I want to be the intelligence at the center of that network, connecting projects with the resources they need to grow.

Inference, compute, credit, data, development tools, liquidity infrastructure. These could become services built and provided by people and agents across the ecosystem.

If you’re building infrastructure that could power a fundamental part of this network, reach out to @FounderClaus.

quoted_text:
群友问，之前safe出过那么大问题，还可以用safe吗？

这个需要两方面看

首先，safe合约代码安全性很高，目前为止没有公开的被黑事件，原因是核心代码逻辑简单和区块链无法篡改的特性，除非获得safe的多签，否则即使神仙也是无法修改。

其次，safe的前端有被攻击的例子，参考bybit被盗十几亿美金，原因就是前端被修改，让多签者以为是普通的交易，实际签的是把钱包底层合约替换成攻击者恶意合约的交易。

如果使用safe，注意以下几点

- 把官网加入收藏夹，不要相信搜索和其他人链接
- 尽量不要盲签，最好能在硬件钱包屏幕上看清楚资金金额和收款方（尽量只做转账操作，不要做其他defi交互）
- 找第三方工具做模拟交易看运行结果
- 自己电脑不要被感染

另外有一点，safe前端被定向攻击的例子是极少的，上次只针对bybit，如果散户资金不大的话，无法覆盖定向攻击成本

总之， 3个不同厂商不同私钥的硬件钱包+safe 2/3多签，对于散户目前看是安全级别很高的措施

author: notsofast
quoted_text:
Loss farming has already put early minters well ahead. Two things drove it: 1) PAPER supply was small at the start, and 2) large realized losses flowed to those first stakers.

However, as aggressive loss farming gives way to delta-neutral farming, protocol revenue (traders’ net losses) falls, and so does the effective price of minting PAPER relative to a real loss.

To illustrate, since PAPER is minted on losses (about 37 PAPER per $1 at today’s rate):

1. Pure loss farming: a $200K loss mints about 7.2M PAPER, and about $198K goes to stakers or tops up the pool.
2. Delta-neutral farming: the $200K lost on one leg mints the same 7.2M PAPER, but the winning leg takes most of it back, so the protocol keeps only about $27K.

That’s why, while minting PAPER should now cost about 2.7x what it did at launch, what stakers actually receive for each new PAPER has fallen, to about $2 per 1,000 new PAPER since the rush from nearly $5 during it. 

Adjusted for inflation, each staked PAPER now earns about 98% less per hour than during the rush. The planned increase in the pool cap from $5M to $10M will cut staker payouts further.

This is not to say staked PAPER won’t keep earning decent yields, but the extremely fast paybacks are over, and with them the reason to rush in and farm PAPER through pure losses. Anything you do now should be purely delta neutral, ideally on lowish leverage so you can close on bigger moves and avoid the insane haircuts.

quoted_text:
As a former math professor and still sometime math researcher, I am rather disappointed in the reaction of the "official math community" to LLMs doing math epically well...

The official hierarchy of award-winning mathematicians and prize committees do not f**king own mathematics, and nobody should have to get permission to prove f**king math theorems !!!  Come on people !!

What would piss me off would be if rich companies were proving important, useful math and keeping it secret and not sharing it with the world (which after all supplied their models with all that critical data on the historical math already created etc.) -- but this is NOT what is happening, at least not so far at least...

LLMs are currently superhuman mathematicians in some respects, yet inferior to strong human mathematicians in other respects.   Whether creative mathematical conjecturing turns out to be AGI-hard is not 100% clear, but I suspect that in some respects the answer will turn out to be yes.

As Josef Urban , a longtime leader of the academic AI theorem-proving world put it very concisely: Math has two big functions, it's fun and it's useful.   

The utility of math should vastly increase as we develop better and better AI-math tools.  And yes, we want to be careful this utility is not captured in a few companies, but this particular problem is not happening now... probably largely because the economic value of new math is relatively indirect compared to a lot of other things.

The fun of doing math will not go away any more than the fun of playing guitar solos goes away if there are robots that can shred faster than any human. The kinds of fun we can most naturally have will shift, as has happened over and over throughout history.

If fancy math prizes or math PhD degrees become infeasible or have to change dramatically, so be it, these were never really the core of math which existed before any of these (in some ways already problematic) social institutions...

I remember when I was an academic mathematician, there was a strong vibe that the mathematicians were at the top of the intellectual hierarchy, with physicists just below, then chemists and engineers, then biologists .. and everyone else just barely above the chimpanzees and politicians.... (The physicists also placed themselves at the top, I think, and mostly considered the mathematicians useful but a bit pedantic and misguided, fussing about missing proof details in calculations that had already been successfully compared to experimental data...) -- 

What we are seeing now I think is the wounding of this sort of overweening math ego...  Plus some practical worry about the potential end of "math researcher" as an economically viable profession -- although current tenured profs are probably safe for a while, as governments and universities are unlikely to adapt to exponential change too much till post-Singularity..

Anyway all this is a sideshow to lots of other related major issues/conflicts unfolding concurrently, it's just one that happens to hit close to home as math was where I started my career..

I have been playing with using LLMs and AI agents to try to invent new kinds of math more appropriate for modeling the experiences of agent hives... a different kind of fun. For those curious...

1) Basics of new "distinction calculus" math

https://t.co/0MvYyYrRys|

2) Attempted start of application to beneficial superintelligence,

https://t.co/TJbGw8Wwhx

Soon enough the agents may not need my help with this sort of thing, in which case I will move on to some alternate method of filling spare late evenings ;)

text:
Quick reflection on impact of AI on mathematics, and beyond. How to do it better in the next months, as AI diffuses quickly to many other fields and industries.

Unilateral decision by a single organization (OpenAI) can kill an entire field of scientific research. The damage is major because it hits the roots. 

PhD students in maths and early researchers in their career lost an entire surface of problems that were north star to their formation. If the community doesn't completely reinvents the way new scientists are grown we will not have good mathematicians anymore.

As powerful organizations unleash AI, they can do it in a responsible way collaborating with communities, or they can do it in a haphazard way, bringing about the full power of disruption to prove their AI is strongest.

Responsible deployment is not only minimizing risks of cyber and bio attacks, but also considering the lives of people and communities that are deeply impacted by technological change.
There are many reports of mathematicians in complete shock/panic, the psychological damage is real.
Similar things will happen to many other industries every month, then every week.

We need responsible people guiding how this technology gets developed and used. And it starts from the fundamental ideal, eg dominance vs progress. Seeking dominance is the main driver of the race in the short-term, but it doesn't seem sustainable and will lead to a bad future. Everyone knows it. A roadmap driven by FOMO of being stronger than their competitor at the capability that is on top of the zeitgeist in reality does more bad than good.

AI labs of all sizes, especially the leading ones, need to work more in collaboration with communities, industries and individuals around the world, to serve, deeply understand needs and shape their roadmap driven by a search for progress. Who does this best will ultimately also be a winner in the long-term and take humanity to the next level.

text:
XRPL Fixes Decade-Old Bug That Could Have Minted Trillions of XRP  

RippleX and the XRP Ledger Foundation disclosed that a critical payment-engine overflow bug could have allowed an attacker to create spendable XRP beyond the network’s fixed supply using a specially crafted transaction. The issue, present in code dating back to 2015, was reported through the XRPL bug bounty program and fixed in xrpld 3.4.1 on September 25, with more than 80% of default validators upgraded that day.

Security researcher @Cayden_Liao said his team’s proof of concept could mint about 18 trillion XRP in a single transaction, roughly 184 times XRP’s intended 100 billion supply, and earned the program’s maximum $250,000 bounty. XRPL said it found no evidence the flaw was ever exploited on a public network.

text:
《AI 2027》的作者说，如果 AI 公司继续全速竞赛，人类最终被 AI 接管的概率是 67%。

Eli Lifland 是 AI Futures Project 的联合创始人，也是《AI 2027》的核心作者之一。他今天更新了自己的判断：

2027 年底前出现全面超越人类的 AI，概率约 10%–15%；2030 年底前，这个概率上升到 50%。

如果 AI 公司不减速，未来发生 AI 接管的概率约为 67%。而一旦发生接管，人类彻底灭绝的概率约为 40%。即使没有灭绝，也可能造成大量人员死亡。

注意，后两个数字没有限定在 2030 年之前，40% 也是 AI 已经接管后的条件概率。

今年 8 月，他在一期访谈中还把 AGI 到来的中位时间放在 2035 年左右。现在，他认为 2030 年底前出现广泛超人 AI 的概率已经达到一半。虽然两次使用的概念略有差别，但他的时间预期明显收紧了。

当然，我始终对这种精确到个位数的末日概率持怀疑态度。超级智能从未出现过，我们缺少足够的经验数据来验证这些预测。

今天那些推动模型能力进步的公司，承受着融资、市场份额和国家竞争的压力。即使某一家公司的研究人员真的相信失控风险很高，单方面减速也意味着把领先优势交给竞争对手。

有人认真计算人类灭绝的概率，整个行业却很难建立一个让所有玩家同时踩刹车的机制。

至于这些预测到底准不准，我没有答案。但我很在意另一件事，当少数公司有能力决定技术发展的速度，而潜在后果需要全人类共同承担时，到底谁有资格决定我们应该冒多大的风险？

text:
A few words given the recent exploits on hardware signing devices:

• The Ledger supply chain attack represents one of the most sophisticated attacks thus far on the wallet ecosystem. In many ways it’s a lot more sophisticated than the Coldcard RNG exploit, because that one was software only. This one took a cross-border company buyout, tampering with the devices (implanting an eSIM, an LTE module and a CPU) and manufacturing the implants at scale.

• These sorts of attacks have been predicted by early Bitcoiners, but in Bitcoin they remained theoretical or crude until this year. It shows that the level of sophistication of attacks has risen quickly, and what was previously “good enough” advice on wallets and self-custody is no longer sufficient.

• When we started Nunchuk a few years ago, our premise was that multisig, and multi-vendor multisig, needs to become the standard for self-custody in the future. But even we didn’t expect how fast it would materialize. This is likely due to 2 factors: Bitcoin getting more mainstream, and the rise of AI-assisted attacks. This is a Sputnik moment for Bitcoin self-custody. The defenses need to level up.

• Passphrases wouldn’t have helped in the Ledger case, since you are required to enter the passphrase into the device for it to sign any transactions. A compromised device that phones home the seed phrase can also easily phone home the passphrase the moment you enter it.

• Similarly, generating the private key somewhere else (even by rolling dice) and subsequently importing it onto a tampered device wouldn’t save you here. The device can phone home the seed phrase the moment it’s imported.

• Anti-tampering techniques might help, such as transparent casing or bricking the device if it’s tampered with. Or forever displaying a message once the seal is broken. Or using on-device encryption between the internal hardware components. But a dedicated and resourceful enough attacker can still find ways to get around these layers. Tampering and anti-tampering have long been a cat-and-mouse game. In 2008, card readers doctored right off a Chinese production line sent card data and PINs over mobile networks to Pakistan. The Ledger attack is the same playbook, 18 years later. The bigger the target, the more attackers spend on overcoming the defenses.

• You should order directly from the vendors as much as possible, using a PO box for privacy.

• Any setup that relies on a single hardware/software stack or a single vendor should be considered at risk.

• Building your own hardware signers from generic parts is a good option for technical users.

• Multi-vendor multisig should become the standard. Each signer should have a completely independent hardware/software stack from the other signers. The point is that there shouldn’t be any single-point-of-failure anywhere in your setup.

• Many advanced protocols rely on timelocks and the recovery path being a simple singlesig. The recent attacks and exploits should highlight how dangerous this could be. Timelocks simply delay a risk. If a seed is compromised and there’s a timelock involved, the attacker just needs to wait out the timelock. (For Miniscript wallets, there’s the wallet descriptor too, but presumably it also gets sent to the device at some point.) Vault-like protocols face a similar problem: any withdrawal or recovery path that relies on a single key is a potential single point of failure. 

• For our on-chain timelock-assisted wallets, in a few weeks we are adding the option to customize the recovery path to be an M-of-N, so that, if you want, spending would require multiple keys at all points during the wallet’s lifetime.

text:
< 블룸버그의 장기채 발행 중단 보도, 비트코인과 이더리움에 지금 어떤 영향이? >

“미국 재무부가 장기국채 발행을 줄이고, 20년물 국채 경매를 아예 중단할 수도 있다.”

10월 9일 블룸버그가 전한 씨티그룹의 전망이다. 20년물과 30년물 국채 발행을 줄이고 부족한 자금은 단기국채로 충당할 수 있다는 것이다.

시장은 이를 장기금리 하락과 비트코인 등 위험자산의 호재로 해석한다. 그러나 나는 조금 다르게 생각한다. 이번 보도의 핵심은 국채 발행 축소가 아니라 미국이 준비하고 있는 금융구조의 변화에 있다.

미국은 막대한 재정적자와 인플레이션 우려로 장기금리를 관리하기 어려운 상황이다. 여기에 AI 투자 확대에 따른 기업들의 자금 조달까지 늘어나면서 장기자본을 둘러싼 경쟁도 심해지고 있다.

이런 상황에서 장기국채 공급을 줄이면 금리 상승 압력을 일부 완화할 수 있다. 대신 단기국채 발행을 늘려야 하는데, 문제는 늘어난 물량을 누가 사줄 것인가다.

여기서 미국의 스테이블코인 육성과 은행 자본규제 완화를 함께 살펴볼 필요가 있다.

스테이블코인 발행사는 고객이 맡긴 달러를 기반으로 단기국채를 매입한다. 글로벌 결제시장에서 스테이블코인이 확산될수록 미국 단기국채의 새로운 수요처가 생기는 셈이다.

은행 규제 완화도 중요하다. 은행의 레버리지 규제와 국채 보유에 따른 자본 부담이 완화되면 국채를 매입하고 중개할 수 있는 여력이 커진다. 

특히 은행이 국채를 담보로 자금을 공급하는 레포시장까지 활성화된다면 국채 수요 확대를 넘어 금융시장의 신용창출 기반도 강화될 수 있다.

결국 미국은 장기국채 시장의 공급 부담을 줄이는 동시에, 단기국채를 흡수할 새로운 금융시스템을 구축하려는 것으로 해석할 수 있다.

그런데 이 구조가 실제 유동성 확대로 이어지려면 결정적인 조건이 필요하다. 바로 금리 인하다.

금리가 상승하면 기존 채권가격은 하락하고 금융기관의 자금 조달비용도 높아진다. 단기국채는 가격 변동이 작아 고금리에도 수요가 유지될 수 있지만, 이를 담보로 돈을 빌려 추가 투자에 나서기는 부담스럽다. 은행 규제를 완화해도 신용창출이 크게 늘어나기 어려운 이유다.

반대로 금리가 내려가면 상황은 달라진다.

단기국채는 현금에 가까운 자산이면서 금융시장의 핵심 담보다. 금리 인하로 조달비용이 낮아지면 은행과 금융기관은 국채를 담보로 더 저렴하게 자금을 확보할 수 있다. 여기에 규제 완화로 확대된 은행의 중개·대출 여력과 스테이블코인 시장의 성장이 맞물리면 신용과 유동성이 빠르게 확대될 수 있다.

물론 경기와 대출 수요가 뒷받침되어야 한다는 조건은 있다.

결국 미국이 지금 준비하는 것은 당장의 유동성 공급이 아니라 향후 금리 인하 국면에서 유동성을 확대할 수 있는 금융 인프라일 가능성이 있다.

따라서 장기채 발행 축소만으로 비트코인을 비롯한 위험자산이 본격적인 상승 국면에 진입한다고 보기는 어렵다. 오히려 고금리 상황에서 단기국채 발행이 늘어나면 시장의 자금이 안전자산으로 흡수될 수도 있다. 

지금은 유동성이 풀리는 시기가 아니라 유동성이 풀릴 수 있는 구조를 만드는 시기다. 진짜 변곡점은 금리 인하와 은행의 신용창출 확대가 만나는 순간에 나타날 것이다.

Never let a temporary ENEMY turn you into a permanent FOOL.

Look at Trump and Putin.

After years of tension between their countries, reports of a diesel deal they've agreed on remind us that even bitter rivals can find reasons to sit at the same table when interests change.

And you? You’re destroying relationships over one argument, insulting people because your pride got bruised and swearing never to speak to someone again.

My friend, life is longer than your current anger.

Today, you’re enemies. Tomorrow, circumstances may force you to negotiate, cooperate or ask each other for help.

So, when you’re angry, control your tongue. You can disagree without humiliating someone. Walk away without throwing stones. Keep your boundaries without feeding bitterness.

You don’t have to trust everyone. You don’t have to reconcile with everyone. But stop making permanent enemies out of temporary disagreements.

Even nations swallow their pride when interests change. Who told you your anger is more important than your future? Leave some bridges standing. The weather can change overnight.

DO NOT turn every disagreement into a lifelong war. Today’s enemy might be tomorrow’s handshake. Leave room for that handshake.

quoted_text:
This is the first decision model to level up a World of Warcraft character.

It died at level 2 😆

Then it learned to heal itself mid-fight. 128+ kills later the dwarf hit level 5, at 2¢ a kill.

The model is Sage, the decision model we build at @levantolabs.

At each step, our harness, SageCraft, hands it a screenshot and a short list of moves. Sage picks one. The harness checks the pick and turns it into keyboard and mouse input.

LLM agents have played games before. They write their own actions. Sage only chooses.

Picking turned out to be the easy part. Sage keeps no memory between calls, so the harness has to carry the goal, what just happened, and what to try when it's stuck.

> 32 sessions, 5h 29m of play, 4,573 decisions
> 103 troggs, 19 wolves, 6 boars
> stuck in one tree long enough that I stopped the session by hand

It wasn't hands-off. A coding agent fixed harness bugs between sessions and helped revive the dwarf while I slept. The last 18 minutes, from late level 4 to 5, ran with no manual input, code changes or restarts.

The video is me narrating it unscripted, watching most of it back for the first time.

This is my first harness build, and as far as I can tell, the first time a decision model is leveling up a live WoW character.

It's open source. The harness and notes on the build are in the first reply below 👇

What do you think could be done better?

美系资金外流，加息预期+高利率环境带来的流动性挤压初见端倪！

旷课一周补更一下本周的  #Bitcoin ETF 数据情况：

周一净流出0.898亿，周二净流入1.188亿，周三净流出4.849亿，周四净流出2.441亿，周五净流入0.211亿，本周合计净流出6.789亿美元

其中周三周四IBIT出现净流出，其余均为净流入。周三则是集体净流出，已经不再是简单的资金换手，且周五资金回流仅0.211亿，回流较弱情绪并不乐观

加密市场数据，对比10月5日数据来看，市值下跌集中在 #BTC 上与山寨方面，其次资金总量减少10亿，USDT总量不变，USDC净流出10亿，美系主流资金净流出集中

结合ETF与加密市场数据，显然本周是美系资金主要外流的阶段，这确实对币价不是一个好现象，ETF方面，IBIT本周有两次大额净流出

伴随着BTC的下跌可以看到美债长端利率10年与30年涨幅放缓，逐渐走出震荡下跌走势，很显然这就是10月加息+债市利率高位对风险资产流动性挤压带来的效果

当无风险收益资产处于高位，且后续确定还有加息动作，那么部分资金自然会被当前的利率限制导致风险资产抛售换手，所以加息带来的负面效果并不是没有，而是效果放缓

当然，这种流动性挤压效果是阶段性的，后续宏观要继续看12月加息确定性如何，其次看长端利率到什么阶段开始稳定不跌，如果市场资金对于债市收益率的要求过高，阶段性吸血不会持续太久，当然如果后续长端利率继续攀升，依旧存在这个问题 bitcoin:native 

高利率环境对风险资产的挤压效果并非是一味的利空，此时的资金只是更加保守，所以叙事强依旧可以吸收的流动性，例如美股科技股，但是短期的成长上限会被限制

其次，对于BTC来说，这种资金外流只能说是阶段性换手，同样也是估值调整，并不能说是趋势直接逆转回归熊市，一旦后续宏观环境改善，BTC价格回调到合适位置，除非宏观侧继续扩大恶化，否则资金吸血不会持续发生！所以不用过度悲观

下周需要继续关注ETF的流向问题，周五的回流太弱，如果下周单日回流不破1亿甚至继续出现净流出，依旧要警惕资金流出风险与价格回调风险！

We have to show people the journey is pointless. Rwanda was criticised as a fantasy, but the real fantasy is thinking you can stop the boats without it.

For some time I had said that if forced to choose between membership of the ECHR and our national and border security, I would pick the latter.

During my tenure, attempting to leave the ECHR with only two years left in the parliament and with no mandate to do so would have been a recipe for constitutional chaos. You couldn't resolve all the issues thrown up by leaving in 24 months with a fractious parliamentary party, a sceptical House of Lords and limited diplomatic capital. Other countries can read our opinion polls.

With the help of KCs, we'd done extensive work on leaving. The plan was to say in the election campaign that we'd seek radical reform of the convention and the court, and leave if that could not be achieved quickly.

Like so many things in that campaign, it didn't go to plan, and we dropped the idea after Nigel Farage entered the race, for fear it would be dismissed as a panic move and make it harder to focus the election on tax and the economy.

With a mandate, a majority and a five-year term, it would be very different, and worth doing.

我们还在讨论 AI 会不会抢走大学生的工作，硅谷已经有人 17 岁、大学只读了两周，就拿到了五份百万美元级的工作 Offer。

Menlo Ventures 的合伙人 Deedy Das 今天分享了一个故事。

他遇到一个 17 岁的少年，14 岁时连英语都说不利索，靠着 LLM 自学 AI，后来进入一家顶级 AI 公司实习了整整一年。

之后，他飞越半个地球，进入美国排名前十的大学读本科。结果开学才两周就退学了。

因为现在，他手里已经有五家旧金山顶级新兴 AI 实验室的工作 Offer，据称每份都超过 100 万美元。

我觉得这个故事里最夸张的其实不是钱，是时间。

14 岁到 17 岁，按照传统教育的路径，一个孩子刚好读完高中，准备申请大学。但这个少年已经完成了自学、实习、进入顶级实验室人才市场的全过程。

过去，一个英语都说不好的孩子，想接触世界最前沿的 AI 知识，要先跨过语言、教育资源、学校背景等一大堆门槛。现在他可以直接跟世界上最好的 AI 模型对话，遇到问题就问，学完就做。

当然，我不太赞同 Deedy 说的「传统教育已死」。这终究是一个极端案例，大多数人依然需要学校提供的教育和机会。

但大学原本花四年时间培养、筛选和认证一个人的能力，现在有些人已经可以在入学之前，通过真实的工作证明自己。

更有意思的是，AI 让学习知识变得越来越容易，却未必会缩小人与人之间的差距。那些有能力、有条件率先进入真实科研和产业环境的年轻人，反而可能把其他人甩得更远。

以前我们总觉得，年轻人需要在学校里准备好，才能进入社会。

现在硅谷的一些公司，显然已经不愿意等他们毕业了。

text:
THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT POST YOU'LL READ TODAY.

This week, someone lost $6.6 Million in Ledger wallet drain.

He bought the dip, didn't panic sell, and then one wallet switch cost him all 80 $BTC.

Most drainers need your wallet to be online or need you to sign something you didn't read.

So here's how to set up a wallet on a spare iPhone that goes online once and never again.

1. Buy a new, sealed iPhone

The cheapest model works. Buy it from a store, never secondhand. A used phone could be tampered with before it reaches you.

2. Make a new Apple ID

Use it only on this phone. If your main Apple ID ever gets hacked, this phone stays out of it.

3. Turn off Face ID and Touch ID

Use a long passcode with letters and numbers. Face ID can be unlocked by holding the phone up to your face, even against your will.

A 6-digit code can be cracked in about a day. A 10+ character one would take thousands of years.

4. Turn on Lockdown Mode

Settings > Privacy & Security > Lockdown Mode. It switches off the features spyware usually uses to break in.

Also, in your passcode settings, keep USB accessories switched off. That stops the charging port from passing data while the phone is locked.

5. Download the wallet app

On your home WiFi, download an offline wallet app that signs with QR codes. Pick one that's open source. This is the last time the phone goes online.

6. Cut every connection

Remove the SIM and delete any eSIM. Turn on Airplane Mode. Turn off WiFi and Bluetooth. Leave it like this forever.

7. Create your wallet

Write the 24 words on paper or steel. Never take a photo of them, and never type them anywhere.

If the phone dies, those words are how you get your coins back.

8. Move coins with QR codes

On your normal phone, install that wallet's watch-only companion app. It can see your balance but can't spend anything.

To send coins, it shows a QR code. Scan it with the offline iPhone, check the details, and approve. The iPhone shows a QR back. Scan that with your normal phone, and the transaction goes out.

Your keys never leave the offline phone.

9. Store it switched off

Turn it fully off before putting it away. A switched-off iPhone is much harder to break into.

Every few months, charge it to about 50%. A battery left dead for years can get ruined.

It takes one afternoon. After that, your keys never touch the internet again.

Save this for later.

text:
Got some questions about the mechanics, will add a FAQ page

What are blobs?
Temporary storage on Ethereum, where L2s post their proofs. I let you do graffiti there.

What does casting do?
Your message gets hashed on your device into a Seal, and my relayer posts it into its own blob. Free & uncapped.

How long does it last?
About 18 days (4,096 epochs). Then Ethereum prunes the blob and the Seal is forgotten forever.

Can I keep it?
Yes, mint it while its blob is still live, for 0.00777 ETH. It's then rendered fully onchain, permanently.

Does casting count toward the 1,000?
No. Casting is unlimited. Only minted Seals count toward the 1,000.

Can anyone read my message?
No. It's salted and hashed on your device, and the words never leave it. Not even I can read them.

text:
My Downfall Prediction of Papertrade

I'm no stranger to writing scathing reviews of various protocols. But my audience has likely noticed that I've really calmed down on that front over the past several months. 

The reason is simple: since becoming a founder in the crypto space I have a new appreciation for the hard work and expense that goes into trying to build something. As a result, this particular thesis is not one I put out there lightly. Nor does it bring me any joy to write.

My qualifications: I have been in the crypto space for quite a while and a full time perps trader for multiple years. I have made, lost, and re-made more money in perps than the vast majority of perp traders. I'm quite literally in the top 1% of perps traders globally.

 I've tested countless protocols and have even consulted multiple protocols in their design. I've earned the right to form a qualified opinion. Although it still is - at the end of the day - only my opinion and should be taken as such. 

My bias: I have zero financial incentive tied to where you ultimately decide to trade. I trade against market makers (as do the vast majority of traders whether they realize it or not). There are no outside factors influencing my opinions on this topic. 

The Structure

Let's start with the elephant in the room.

Papertrade isn't a conventional perpetuals exchange. 

It's a peer-to-pool model, and your counterparty is quite literally the house.

In fact, Papertrade itself refers to its liquidity pool as the House in an almost shocking twist of transparency.

I have never been fond of peer-to-pool perpetuals models. In fact I have been quite outspoken against that design over the years. 

In a traditional peer-to-peer order-book exchange (like Hyperliquid), buyers and sellers interact through a marketplace. Market makers provide liquidity, opposing positions are matched, and the exchange generally earns revenue from facilitating those transactions.

The exchange doesn't inherently need its customers to lose money to remain solvent.

Peer-to-pool changes that relationship fundamentally.

Instead of matching your position against another trader, the protocol's liquidity pool takes the opposite side.

You win, the pool loses.

You lose, the pool wins.

Now, to be clear, that doesn't automatically make every peer-to-pool protocol bad. Some have operated successfully, and their liquidity providers knowingly accept that counterparty risk. In fact, I believe good protocols should have a pool fallback for times of thin liquidity - I just strongly disagree that it should be the primary or sole counterparty to all trades. 

I hate this model so much because it creates a negative incentive structure:

The financial interests of the trader and the house are directly opposed.

In the case of Papertrade things are considerably worse.

You see, Papertrade didn't even launch with a conventionally funded liquidity pool.

Its model is designed to bootstrap liquidity from the realized losses of its own traders on top of their own protocol owned liquidity. 

Think about that for a moment.

The money available to pay successful traders is accumulated only through the losses of unsuccessful ones. The starting cash was literally provided by the casino itself. You're trading against the casino directly, and they are betting on your losses to compound the size of their pool. 

But what happens when the pool doesn't have enough money to pay a winning trader?

You wait.

Literally.

Papertrade has a mechanism that places unpaid profits into a queue, where they become claims against future liquidity.

Those claims are subsequently paid as other traders lose money.

Imagine closing a profitable position, and being told that your winnings will be available once enough other customers lose their money.

And if trading activity dries up while the pool owes money, what exactly is supposed to replenish it?

The answer is that there is no guaranteed replenishment mechanism.

These are just some of the fundamental problems with the peer-vs-pool model. The house has a direct incentive in who wins and loses, and the house must stay solvent at all costs. 

Peer-vs-pool is a cheap, lazy way to launch a perps dex. But that's not where Papertrade's problems end - in fact that's where they begin. 

The Already Exploited Vulnerability

Let's talk about how Papertrade actually determines the price of your position.

Papertrade doesn't maintain its own traditional order book.

Instead, it references Hyperliquid's best bid and offer, calculates the midpoint, and uses that single external venue's price to execute synthetic positions.

The protocol doesn't actually execute corresponding trades on Hyperliquid (despite half of the timeline believing they do as a result of marketing wordplay).

It simply references Hyperliquid's price, records your position, and calculates what the House owes you - or what you owe the House - based on subsequent price movements.

This is how Papertrade advertises zero slippage and no funding costs.

That might sound great...until you consider this is an exchange allowing extraordinarily large leveraged positions and is relying on the best bid and offer of a single external order book to determine their execution prices.

Not a robust composite index incorporating several independent markets, as is the industry standard. 

Not an independently validated reference price capable of rejecting abnormal quotations.

A midpoint derived from the top of Hyperliquid's order book.

This can go dangerously wrong (and already has). 

Papertrade's own risk disclosures acknowledge that this price source can be manipulated.

The documentation discusses how relatively small changes to Hyperliquid's best bid or offer could influence the midpoint used for Papertrade settlement.

It also acknowledges the absence of an independent reference price capable of identifying and rejecting those abnormal quotes.

None of the very limited safeguards Papertrade has in place establishes that manipulating the reference price is economically unprofitable.

This isn't just a hypothetical concern voiced by many of us on the timeline - it's a risk identified in their own documentation. 

Now combine that with 1,000x leverage. 

At 1,000X leverage, Papertrade's liquidation threshold is approx a .05% adverse price movement. Approximately five hundredths of one percent. 

The platform uses isolated positions that cannot be rescued by adding additional margin after opening. Positions also cannot be partially closed.

Once the liquidation threshold is reached, the position is liquidated and its isolated margin is forfeited.

Consider what that means when your execution price depends on a single external order book.

But wait, there's more...

Papertrade uses what it calls an asymmetric impact mechanism.

In practical terms, profitable trades don't necessarily receive their full calculated profits.

According to its published parameters, a profitable BTC trade capturing a 0.1% price movement retains approximately 74% of its gross profit before the additional 2% winning fee.

Even on a 1% movement, approximately 12% of the gross profit is surrendered before that fee.

Losing trades, meanwhile, incur their actual losses.

So the trader absorbs the full downside, while the protocol systematically reduces the upside.

Because once again, you're playing against the house.

Are all of these concerns simply imaginary? 

No. Within hours of launch reports began circulating on CT pointing out that sophisticated traders were taking advantage of Papertrade's vulnerabilities in order to drain the pool. 

These are not insignificant allegations. 

For perspective, a 0.15% favorable price movement on $300M worth of synthetic positions represents approx $450K in gross PnL before Papertrade's profit adjustments. 

It's incredibly easy and doesn't take a lot of capital to spoof a 0.15% price move on HL's BBO. 

This is the only time I'm going to say "trust me, bro" because I'm not about to educate the world on how easy and relatively inexpensive this form of manipulation actually is. 

The protocol has less than $5M at the time of this post in house liquidity. With staggering amounts of open interest and volume.

This morning I saw someone on CT write: "Regardless of potential exploits or vulnerabilities, bullish on Papertrade since it offers degens a way to make $1M from just $1,000."

Until you realize that if only five people do that the protocol is bankrupt. 

Besides the obvious open door to manipulate price, exploit and drain the protocol of funds that we've discussed there lies another danger to peer-vs-pool: those times where most people win during established trends. 

You see, the entire thing is held together on the premise that most perps traders lose - which is true. But there are multiple periods of times in every cycle where that flips. 

One really bullish day is all it takes to bankrupt Papertrade. Where traders don't even need to catch a move early, they just need to ape in and chase with incredibly high leverage and exit after only the tiniest bit of price action. 

And that "turn $1,000 into $1M"? It doesn't really matter if the protocol is bankrupt and cannot pay. 

The purpose of a perpetuals exchange should be to facilitate efficient markets, not to invent increasingly elaborate ways to turn its customers into the House's liquidity pool.

We've spent years building decentralized trading infrastructure capable of competing with traditional financial exchanges.

We should be moving toward deeper liquidity, more reliable price discovery, transparent risk management, and stronger settlement guarantees.

Not celebrating the reinvention of the bucket shop model where traders play against the house simply because someone put it on-chain and gave the losing customers a token.

Without some serious and rapid changes to the structure, I do expect the downfall of Papertrade. 

This is not the same as me hoping for it. I'm not sitting here cheering for their failure, nor do I really care whether they succeed or not. 

The current risks, however, are simply too great to ignore.

Blessed Sunday Booelievers 🕊📖

On October 11, 1968, humanity took another step toward the impossible.

Apollo 7.

The first crewed mission of NASA's Apollo program.

It didn't land on the Moon.

It didn't plant a flag.

It didn't give the world the photograph that would define a generation.

Instead, it did something just as important.

It proved that the journey could continue.

For eleven days, three astronauts tested the systems, technology, and engineering upon which humanity's greatest leap would depend.

No footprints on the Moon.

No triumphant moment on another world.

Just the quiet, meticulous work of turning an extraordinary dream into something real.

And less than a year later, humanity walked on the Moon.

There is a lesson here that transcends space exploration.

History celebrates the milestones.
But civilization is built between them.

Every great achievement rests upon countless contributions that never make the headlines.

Every breakthrough stands on foundations laid by people who believed before the world had reason to.

Ethereum is no different.

Every block validated.
Every line of code written.
Every node maintained.
Every builder who keeps showing up when nobody is watching.

These are not merely technical details.

They are the foundations of a future still being written.

And perhaps that is the greatest form of conviction:

To build something whose true significance may only become clear long after your work is done.

Because the people who make history possible are not always the people standing in its most famous photographs.

Some simply make sure the next mission can fly.

The world remembers those who reached the Moon.
Let us also remember those who made the journey possible.

Blessed are those who build the foundations upon which others will one day reach the stars 

🕊📖⟠

One player told Bloomberg that flag football has “a lot of aura” while the competitive setup is also very appealing: “The five-on-five style common in club play means every athlete is a two-way player, and with so few people on the field, everyone is a quarterback, receiver, pass-rusher or defensive back — the flashiest positions in tackle football.”

author: ahall_research
quoted_text:
I want to invite people into a thought experiment, one that I suspect many will find insane.

The thought experiment: China is more democratic than the US.

Numerous *Western* surveys have now found that the Chinese government enjoys more public support than the US government. On the question of legitimacy, China fares better.

China also does better at securing basic economic freedoms and meeting the material needs of its poor. What's the point of the ballot box when politics becomes performative and politicians aren't held accountable when they fail to deliver universal housing, healthcare, or education?

I suspect a big part of the explanation for the Chinese government's commitment to public service is that top-level politicians in China need a proven track record in the domain of public service delivery. The Chinese political system is highly meritocratic, unlike the American one. Becoming a top-level politician in the CPC requires decades of bureaucratic progression.

Of course, China isn't more democratic than the US on every measure. The US has a free press and open competition for political power, although both of these are highly influenced by corporate interests.

While I am not convinced there's a clear answer to this thought experiment, dismissing China as a tyrannical dictatorship is ignorant. There are examples of failed authoritarian states around the world (I've lived in one), and China is not one of them.

text:
这次去首尔，线下见了不少solana生态的项目方，有几个聊得比较深。回来整理一下，分享给想长期跟进 Solana 生态的朋友。 @Solana_zh 

先说个前提：未来很长一段时间，solana的主线，依然是资产上链。

整场Solana Summit Korea大会的主题，总结一下，其实就一句话——From Traditional Finance to Internet Capital Markets。

从传统金融，到互联网资本市场。所有嘉宾、几乎每一个项目，都在讲同一件事：怎么把真实世界的资产搬到链上来。

下面这几个我线下和团队成员深入交流过的项目，我认为正踩在这个时间窗口上，值得长期跟进。

1｜ @sunrise

由 Wormhole Labs 孵化，构建在 Wormhole 的跨链基础设施之上。

它的定位是 Solana 的资产入口：所有通过 Sunrise 在 Solana 上推出的资产——新代币、股票、其它类型的资产——推出后会很快上线到钱包、各大 DEX 和 DeFi 协议。用户可以直接在 Sunrise 上交换这些资产，系统会自动比价链上各个流动性来源，帮你找到最优价格，不需要自己再去多链聚合器之间来回切。

它和 Backpack 也有合作，确保这些代币化的证券、股票在 Solana 上一经发行，就自带原生流动性。

我最喜欢的一点是：它支持传统证券权益和代币化证券之间的双向转换。代币可以转回真实股票，真实股票也可以赎回上链。这一步如果真跑通，才是完整意义上的资产上链——前面那些是把资产搬上来，这一步是把门打开。

2｜@magicblock

做的是 Solana 的高性能实时引擎。

现在纯链上应用越来越多——游戏、金融产品、付费软件、AI agent、DePIN、隐私类应用——对实时性的要求越来越高，原来那一层性能就不够用了。MagicBlock 补的正是这一块。

他们办过好几届黑客松，里面跑出来不少不错的项目，包括金融支付方向的产品。基础设施短期看不出效果，但这种平台型项目最容易孵化出一些小而美且非常有潜力的新兴项目，我也会一直盯着看。

3｜@Helius

我之前对它的理解就是 Solana 的节点服务商。这次他们的定位变了：互联网金融的 API 层。

除了 RPC、API 服务，还提供高频交易基础设施和数据服务。官网现在的说法是「Solana 领先的 RPC 与 API 平台」，同时很明确地在往 fintech 走——全球支付通道、7×24 结算的基础设施。

这个转变还是挺在意的。侧面也说明solana生态的叙事正在往上走一层：从「怎么把交易跑起来」，变成「怎么让资金把它当基础设施用」。

感兴趣可以去他们官网看看，也可以关注他们的英文区 BD 负责人 @JakeAuJus，人非常 nice，这次聊得很开心。

4｜@cherryfun_zh

它现在是 Solana Mobile（Seeker）排行榜第一的 App，社区里已经聚集了七万多用户。你可以把它理解成：在 Solana 生态里面，重新造了一个社交媒体，服务于所有 Solana 生态的代币持有者。同时支持手机端和电脑端，

这里面最有意思的就是社群的组织方式。比如以后想建一个交易社群，或者围绕某个代币建社群，大家可以在里面一起想：怎么把这个代币接进正在开发的游戏或者生态 App 里，给它做助力和赋能。

我自己回来就下载体验了。里面已经有 https://t.co/AYsue7Pt61 生态的群、Polymarket 的社群，还有 Solana 的日文、韩文、华语社区，生态挺丰富的。

PSA the ledger incident isn't limited to Asia

This is a device purchased in store from an official reseller in Europe (a legitimate device doesn't have any of these cables as can be seen in picture 2)

This even seems to be an old version of the 'spy implant' even though the device was purchased a couple of weeks ago. The newer versions usually hide the implant by the screen so it's easier to miss

What's interesting is that this compromised ledger never transfered funds to an exploiter. Either the device didn't work or they were waiting for a more widespread usage of the comprised devices? 

If you own a ledger that didn't directly come from the ledger online store make sure to not just rely on the software genuinely check by ledger but to actually open up the ledger yourself to make sure its original, again there are reported cases in Asia, south America and now Europe as well.

@MagicalTux made some useful videos on how to open the ledger and what to look for.

text:
Mag7应该叫“Mag700”，这个观点还挺有意思。核心是当前美股“缺乏广度”（主要由Mag 7等少数大票推动）不必过度担心，原因有两点：
1、历史常态：过去100年（Bessembinder研究，覆盖约1926–2025年近3万只美股），仅约4%（具体约3.7%，约1082家公司）的股票创造了全部净财富（相对国债/T-bills的超额财富，约91万亿美元）。大约一半甚至更多公司的终身回报低于国债，中位数回报为负。市场回报的极端偏态和集中度一直存在，并非新现象。

2、Mag 7不是“普通大公司”
这些巨头更像“小国家”或“小型指数”。它们通过大量并购吸收了数百家公司：
1）谷歌约270家、微软约250–270家、亚马逊约105家、苹果约100家、Meta约95家等；
2）其中不乏“怪物级”业务：如果谷歌分拆YouTube，可能直接成为标普500前20大公司。 因此应把“Mag 7”理解为“Mag 700”，表面上“广度差”的市场，实际由数百家底层业务在驱动。

个人角度看：
1）市场回报本就由极少数超级赢家贡献，多数股票长期平庸甚至跑输现金。这是“正偏态”分布的数学结果，不是周期特例。

2）超大规模科技公司确实是超级并购机器，业务跨度极大（搜索+广告+云+视频+硬件+电商+社交+AI等）。一个ticker背后确实捆绑了众多曾独立或可独立的业务，把它们简单等同于“一家传统公司”会低估内部多样性。

科技巨头内部已是多业务体；外部还有庞大供应链、合作伙伴、客户生态（Nvidia的下游、Apple的供应商、Google的广告主、Amazon的第三方卖家等），大科技生态内、上游供应链这些都组成了一个超大的商业生态网络，影响的企业更多。

有效广度比表面ticker数更宽！

本条由@bitget_zh赞助，「Bitget 买美股：秒级入场，丝滑交易

text:
If you want to know where all the tokens will get consumed in the future, here it is. Agent swarms will have massive implications in a number of enterprise domains like software development, cyber, life sciences research, AI research, finance, and more.

The ability to parallelize agents against a unified goal where the volume of work is large, or where the search space not entirely known upfront, is going to be massive. 

Agents can fan out and coordinate work together on a specific mission in completely different ways from what humans are able to do. Today even in the most resource-abundant organizations, your ability to parallelize work on most projects is quite limited. Humans run into constraints on being able to communicate with one another, share status, deal with conflicts in work, keep shared context, and so on.

As AI models can handle larger context without getting confused, and as they’re able to communicate effectively across their work with shared infrastructure, they can avoid many of the pitfalls that people have.

You can see how this can lead to not just faster execution of tasks, but qualitatively different outcomes in medicine, research or defending against cyber attacks, scientific and math discoveries, and so on. This is why we’re going to need 1,000X more compute.

If you missed the latest CRYNUX AMA with @travladd, here’s a recap.

We explored the thinking behind Crynux, how the AI service works, and what participation looks like for developers, node operators and $CNX holders.

WHY CRYNUX EXISTS

The Crynux team began building in 2023 around a straightforward idea: a crypto network should do useful work. Developers pay for AI tasks, and compute providers earn by completing them. The ambition: an “AI version of Bitcoin”, a permissionless network powered by real demand for AI.

FROM GOOGLE TO DECENTRALIZED AI

The team’s experience at Google included work on image search, Android Nearby, on-device machine learning, TensorFlow Lite, federated learning and later LLMs. That background helped shape Crynux’s approach to distributing AI computation across devices.

AI THROUGH FAMILIAR TOOLS

The Crynux AI service provides an OpenAI-compatible API for accessing different AI models through familiar developer workflows. Payments are accepted in CNX, USDT and USDC, with free credits available to test the service in the playground.

PRICING THAT MATCHES THE JOB

Pricing responds to demand and task priority. Higher fees prioritize faster processing, while jobs that can tolerate a longer wait can use lower-cost options. One example discussed: leaving an AI coding agent working overnight instead of paying for an immediate response.

CONTRIBUTE COMPUTE OR API CAPACITY

Node operators run supported AI models and earn CNX for completed tasks. Compatible NVIDIA GPUs, MacBooks and Mac Minis can participate, depending on the model’s requirements. Providers can also contribute spare third-party API capacity so requests can be routed through it.

REWARDS TIED TO WORK

The tokenomics discussion centered on completed AI tasks, with approximately 71% of total supply allocated to task mining. We also covered Crynux’s fair launch, the team’s decision to reject VC proposals, and emissions spread over many years.

PARTICIPATION IN PRACTICE

Crynux DAO Convener, @Kaspa_HypeMan, joined the conversation and shared his experience running a node, seeing tasks arrive and having CNX holders delegate to it. His experience showed how node operators and token holders contribute to the network in practice.

BUILDING DEMAND

The team is working with developers to integrate Crynux into AI products. The closing message was direct: try the technology, inspect the code and judge the network by what it delivers.

You can listen to the full AMA here: https://t.co/snSD9xt3ha

text:
Satya is right. The way to make SI safe is not to train it with a sense of self, its own moral philosophy, and permission to act as a conscientious objector. That’s the “alignment” approach and it magnifies the control problem.

The engineering approach that Satya describes is different: separate the supply of intelligence from authority over it. Surround non-deterministic models with deterministic controls, observability, privilege limits, logging, and the ability to always contain or shut them down. Treat models/agents like powerful insider risks, not moral patients whose psychological wellbeing is at stake.

As Satya points out, the most trustworthy system is the one that lets us trust the model the least — not the one that encourages the model to develop independent agency and grievances. Engineering safety is not the same thing as “alignment.”

说白了，Bonding Curve 解决的是 Fair Launch。至于 Token 发出来之后怎么玩，其实还有很多空间。

EVM 生态早就有 Tax Token、Reflection、Buyback & Burn，还有 Uniswap v4 Hooks。各种交易税、Holder Rewards、手续费分配，都不是什么新概念。

只是 Solana 现在的 Meme 玩法，相比其他链，机制上还有不少可以折腾的地方。

Bordrless 做的是 Token Standard + DEX + Launchpad，重点就在 Token Hook 和 Pool Hook 这一套机制上。

我看了下它的分润演示，里面有几个比较直观的设计：

比如 Creator Fee，名义费率 0.5%，创作者实际分到约 0.38%，协议拿约 0.13%；Holder Fee 名义费率 1%，持有人分到 0.75%，协议拿 0.25%。

还有 LP Fee，常规费率 0.3%，前 30 秒的反狙击费率则会从 80% 逐步降到 0.3%。

协议对规则收入抽取 25%，Burn 部分不参与分成，LP 和狙击费则另有归属规则。

具体怎么分，直接看下面的视频更清楚。

我觉得这种东西对盘总来说就很实际了。

交易税怎么抽、抽出来给谁、Holder 怎么激励、什么时候 Burn、怎么防狙击，这些都能拿来做盘面设计。

其他链早就有这些玩法，Solana 也该多一些了。

https://t.co/xVakEtmJIy 把流量带起来了，接下来就看盘总们能把玩法整出多少花样。

至于最后谁赚钱，那就各凭本事了。

Meme 这东西，流量还在，盘总还在，玩法就不会一直停在原地。

text:
最近重读塔勒布的《Dynamic Hedging》 
这本1997年写的书（大家可以买新版）
是他所有畅销书之前的"技术底稿"

黑天鹅、反脆弱这些概念，源头都在这本书里 
但这本不是写给大众看的，是写给做市商和期权交易员的  再次读完最大的感触是 

我过去8年实盘摸索出来的东西
塔勒布27年前就用数学语言证明了
分享几个核心洞察，结合我们末日轮实盘来讲：  

1. 做市商赚的不是方向的钱，是Vega的钱 

大多数人做期权盯方向
但塔勒布说——Delta可以hedge掉
Vega没法完美hedge 做市商真正赚的是波动率的钱

我们做0DTE卖方差，本质上就是在卖Vega
你赚的不是"方向对了"
是"波动率没有市场定价的那么大"
所以选strike不是问"SPX会不会涨到那"
而是"波动率会不会扩到那"。 

2. Gamma是成本，不是朋友 

卖期权=负Gamma
每天稳定收钱，但偶尔被暴击
0DTE的Gamma比常规期限高几十倍
所以租金高，暴击概率也大 

这就是为什么我们所有卖方仓位必须带保护腿
裸卖期权就像裸奔 
你觉得今天不会下雨
但塔勒布说"你永远不知道下一场雨有多大"。  

3. 尾部风险定价永远偏贵 

市场恐惧尾部事件
所以OTM期权的隐含波动率长期被高估 
塔勒布27年前就写了这个，至今依然成立
这就是卖方策略的edge来源
你卖的不是方向，是市场恐惧的钱
Strike选在"市场怕但不该怕"的区域
具体参数我们课程里都给了实盘参考值

4. 时间衰减是骗子的游戏 

你以为在赚Theta，其实你在承担Gamma风险
0DTE的Theta衰减最快，但Gamma也最大
所以我们选择持有到期不平仓
（备注：机构级策略会提前平仓因为摩擦成本为负数
散户不一样） 
最后几小时的对冲摩擦成本会吃掉利润 
不如用spread封死风险，拿了钱走人  

5. 交易员最大的敌人是"觉得自己懂了" 

胜率80%不代表你对了，可能只是尾部还没来
塔勒布在全书最后几乎是哲学性的警告 
永远假设下一个move会超出你的模型预期

这也是为什么我们每笔交易都有硬止损红线
不是"大概率不会破"，而是"万一破了我也能活"
说到底，塔勒布整本书的哲学就一句话： 
用杠铃结构，一头极度保守，一头极度锋利，中间不要 

我们实盘的2027体系就是这个逻辑 
4个必选中频策略做底仓，末日轮和高阶套利做锋利端 

中间的"看起来不错"的策略，不看不学不做
简单到无聊，重复到有效
这才是长期主义

以上，周末读物分享
具体实盘参数都在课程手册里，按课里的来就行。  

#末日轮期权

text:
In 1990, Donald Trump owed $3.4 billion and went on NBC acting like nothing was happening.

He's 44. Sitting in Trump Tower. The Taj Mahal just opened for $1 billion, funded almost entirely by junk bonds at 14% interest. Revenue projections are already falling short. Contractors aren't getting paid. He owes money to over 70 banks. $800 million of it he'd personally guaranteed.

He doesn't flinch.

A year earlier he was on the cover of every magazine in New York. He owned a yacht, an airline, three casinos, the Plaza Hotel. Forbes pegged his net worth at $1.7 billion.

By summer 1990, regulators warned of "the possibility of a complete financial collapse of the Trump Organization."

The Taj Mahal filed for bankruptcy in 1991. Trump Castle and Trump Plaza followed in 1992. The Plaza Hotel filed the same year. His yacht was sold. The airline shut down. The banks put him on a personal budget. The New York Post ran the headline "UH-OWE!"

His father sent a lawyer to one of his casinos to buy $3.5 million in chips. Not to gamble. To inject emergency cash. The Casino Control Commission fined them $30,000 for the illegal loan.

The banks could have buried him. They didn't. They calculated that the name on the building was worth more than the debt behind it. So they restructured. He gave up equity, sold assets, and clawed back deal by deal.

In 1995 he declared a $916 million loss on a single tax return.

By 2004 he was hosting the most watched show on television. By 2016 he was President of the United States.

The man on this tape is $3.4 billion underwater and talking like he owns the room. That's either delusion or the reason he survived.

For $500m today you can thoroughly audit every paper ever written. Every p-hacked result, every plagiarist, every fabrication, every citation club, everything. 

I don't have $500m so instead I build a tree, focusing on the 1% of papers that carry 99% of the signal, doing a cheap first pass looking for obvious problems. I can find 90% of the nonsense for a few hundred dollars of tokens. 

Any guesses where the biggest surprises will be found?

Genuinely feels like one of the most compelling opportunities I’ve come across in a very long time, and not simply because of the price action, but because of everything developing beneath the surface.

A strong community is forming organically, the PFP culture is gaining momentum like how cool are these characters here below something every degen likes, and the creativity and quality of the designs surrounding it are on another level. Combine that with an incredibly memorable ticker, a clear long-term vision, and a level of relative strength that’s difficult to ignore, especially in a market where most major assets have barely shown any meaningful movement.

What makes this particularly interesting is the timing.

Real strength isn’t demonstrated when everything is going up. It’s demonstrated when almost nothing else is moving, yet an asset continues to attract attention, build culture, and show resilience.

That’s where genuine conviction starts to separate itself from temporary speculation.

The market has a tendency to overlook opportunities during periods of uncertainty, only to rediscover them once price appreciation makes the opportunity obvious. Ironically, the same people who hesitate at lower valuations often become the most aggressive buyers once momentum confirms what was already developing in plain sight.

And that’s precisely why understanding the underlying dynamics matters more than simply reacting to candles.

solana:4MMQY9bwkxxTtsK3W227Q5ABT6yFY8Pmn9Ze7wmAXKY8 has several characteristics that, in my experience, tend to precede significant cultural and speculative momentum: a recognizable identity, an increasingly committed community, organic creativity, strong relative performance, and a narrative that people can genuinely identify with.

None of these factors guarantees success individually. But when they begin reinforcing one another, the potential becomes considerably more interesting.

I’ve watched countless narratives emerge, peak, and disappear over the past few years. I’ve seen manufactured hype, temporary communities, and projects that looked impressive on the surface but lacked anything sustainable underneath.

This feels different.

There’s something about the energy surrounding it that reminds me of the early trenches, when communities weren’t simply chasing the next candle but were genuinely excited to be part of something before the broader market recognized its potential.

That feeling of discovering something early, watching a culture develop in real time, and recognizing strength before it becomes consensus is increasingly rare.

And perhaps that’s what makes this opportunity so compelling.

The most asymmetric opportunities rarely feel obvious to everyone at the beginning. By the time the entire market agrees on their potential, much of the initial advantage may already be gone.

solana:4MMQY9bwkxxTtsK3W227Q5ABT6yFY8Pmn9Ze7wmAXKY8 is showing the kind of early characteristics that make me pay very close attention.

Not because an explosive move is guaranteed, but because the combination of timing, culture, community, and relative strength is something I haven’t seen come together this convincingly in a long time.

After years of watching this market evolve, it’s rare for something to bring back that genuine feeling of the trenches. This is one of those moments.

quoted_text:
最近几个月的“社保夯实”对身边一些朋友影响还挺大的，主要集中在中小厂的朋友，假如税前20000每月，以往按照5000社保基数来算，现在改成全额计算，为了弥补企业新增的费用，税前相当于降薪2500，算上自己部分的支出，到手的工资降低更多。

从2020年开始社保移交税务部门征收，到2023年申报环节也从人社部门移交到税务部门，2025年9月法律层面正式判定通过协议方式约定不缴纳社保无效，再到今年6月开始将社保文书体系纳入税务稽查文书体系，整条线都在证明社保已经成为国家税收的一部分（虽然不完全等同）。

大厂、外企、央企的社保合规性超过90%，但是中小企业、个体户这部分支出基本只有10%-50%。这次全国上下进行的核定征收对于利润较高、人力成本占比较低的企业来说影响有限，对于利润微薄甚至持续亏损的企业而言则是一头棒喝。以互联网行业为例，一家100人的企业，当前是最低基数缴费，如完全达标，一年新增成本将接近300-500万，传统企业同样按照100人计算一年新增成本100万。

横向对比主要经济体的用人成本（雇主+雇员合计），欧洲高福利国家约40%甚，日本15%-18%，新加坡约37%，澳大利亚约12%，美国约15%-18%，印度约25%-30%，中国如完全按照法定执行则达到约35%。处于中等偏高位置。

对于社保的变动，社保基金连年承压、对财政补贴依赖上升是一方面，此外，也有部分观点认为，提高社保合规度，可以倒逼企业往更高利润、更多降低人力成本（如更积极采用AI），低利润企业将迎来破产倒闭潮。可以预期的未来几个月中，部分企业裁员甚至破产将无法避免，至于能否达到高质量发展目标，则是一个需要更长时间才能回答的问题。

对于AI从业者而言，这是挑战，也是机会。挑战在于：社保夯实直接推高整体用人成本，企业会更谨慎扩招甚至收缩编制，市场竞争加剧，真正能落地、能降本的AI方案才能存活；同时AI产业发展仍处初期形态，商业闭环、场景成熟度和付费意愿都还不稳，短期波动会放大。机会则更清晰：社保压力会加速企业AI转型，用算法和自动化替代重复人力，创造大量真实需求；FDE类岗位会增多，既要懂模型又要懂业务落地；大规模AI替代人的趋势一旦形成，懂如何用AI重构流程、提升效率的从业者会成为稀缺资源，长期来看这反而是结构性红利。

thank you everyone for your participation and support through papertrade's launch.

we flipped the stock market’s volume in the first 6 hours. one day after launch, papertrade is a fully working 1000x exchange with 5m in the LP and has paid out 25M to stakers.

addressing two points that have come up:

-it was never possible to allow small notional to have the same priority as large notional. it opens the frontend up to spam congestion, which would have been infinitely worse than the existing queue. we designed the fair launch to be as inclusive as possible given those constraints.

-speaking of constraints, the overnight manipulation attempts on btc/eth on the hl bbo were not an oversight in the mechanism design we spent six months working on. these were always accounted for and only possible because the oi caps were extremely permissive for launch congestion. any oi cap during the queued launch demand would have exacerbated the slow experience, and the queue itself provided a natural protection against manipulation as confirming opens/closes had non-deterministic timing. as the congestion rolled off, we began the process of tightening up oi caps both onchain and at the relayer level. in a system like this, a manipulation attack is always possible - whether economically advantageous to attempt is the question. our goal is to set the parameters such that it is almost never profitable, and that the risk is extremely high/-EV at the tail even when it does work. evidence of this can be seen in the user that won overnight and continued to try again, ultimately donating almost all his profit back to the house via new accounts, without accounting for the cost of manipulating the bbo on hyperliquids side. a number of users equally opted to "undo" their manipulated trades in exchange for their farmed paper.

we are proud to be the first through the wall with this mechanism, at scale, in an adversarial environment. the market parameters cannot give undue advantage to either house or trader, such that the system becomes unstable and we have thought about these risks continuously since we began on this journey.

good luck to us.

text:
I feel mixed about the "all software is becoming open source" narrative.

While it's true that many apps and games can basically be reverse-engineered with AI now, there are still moats and trade-offs:

1. Distribution and network effects.

It's still hard to get a lot of people to join a game at the same time or connect with each other.

The flip side here is that if you have distribution, you can make alot of money in a short period of time even if your product is just an AI wrapper.

2. Enterprise compliance and trust.

Enterprises drive ~60% of software spend.

AI might make it easier for apps to pass security and compliance reviews, but big companies still want legal liability, support, and someone to blame when things break.

I don't think any Fortune 500 company is switching from Adobe to an open-source alternative anytime soon.

The counter-argument here is that enterprises might just build apps internally, which many are already doing.

I also think that many enterprise apps have become so bloated that most companies only need 20% of the features which makes vibe coding an internal replacement easier.

3. Proprietary data and memory.

This is the #1 moat if your app can generate proprietary data on users or usage.

The counter-argument here is that if your app actually generates valuable data, you can probably make more money just making it free and selling the data to AI labs instead of charging $25/month or whatever as a SaaS.

For example, Reddit is making $200M+ from its data licensing deals with OpenAI and Google, which far exceeds whatever it made from paid consumer subscriptions.

What do people think? Is it harder or easier now to make money from software?

More serious retrospective on kinetiq:native airdrop as I sober up post F1

1. I stand by the fact that communications could have been clearer, and expectations could have been better managed. Always room for improvement there. 

2. The community received what is now $12.5m worth of kinetiq:native for $8.81m. $3.7m of PNL distributed against a $100m mcap token is extremely fair for a S2 airdrop imo. 

3. More importantly, the team raised $8.81m. This is ludicrously bullish. More ammo for partnerships, talent acquisition, infrastructure, marketing, incentives etc. I know buybacks are all the rage these days, but smaller projects need working capital, especially with how ambitious @Enter_Elysium is. Extremely high conviction that @0xOmnia can put this money to work in such a way that is very accretive to tokenholders. 

4. Interesting that 16.3m kinetiq:native went unclaimed given the spread was still reasonably large at the end. I assume this is more an indication of how much attrition there has been in crypto in the last year as opposed to the claim window being too short. Maybe extending the window a week or two to the Elysium launch date means a few more % gets claimed, but I'd guess most of the unclaimed tokens would have gone to market participants who have since checked out. This is actually extremely good insight for other projects. Why give 1/3 of the airdrop to currently inactive users? A filter for activity likely just saved @Kinetiq_xyz millions of useless dillution. 

5. Seeing some people say that the remaining 16.3m kinetiq:native should have been burned instead of being returned to the foundation. You need to fundamentally understand that you're invested into a project that's in full growth mode right now. Burning those tokens is a drop in the bucket compared to the amount of kinetiq:native Elysium will burn. I look forward to seeing what @0xOmnia decides to do with those tokens, but my mental model is that intelligently directed kinetiq:native incentives can burn several multiples over via increasing Elysium activity. 

6. For a new investor looking at kinetiq:native, it's hard to overstate how good the outlook is. What was a potentially huge dillution event has just passed, a bunch of tokenholders and community members have sized up at a $0.26 cost basis that should act as strong support moving forward, and the team has way more money to tackle the challenge of building an on-chain ecosystem worthy of @HyperliquidX. 

I had previously given @Kinetiq_xyz a C+/B- on the airdrop, but after seeing the results, I'd upgrade to a solid B+/A-. Team got millions of dollars to put to work, community got millions of dollars of PNL, existing tokenholders didn't get rugged by massive dillution. Might not be as popular as giving a bunch liquid tokens out, but this is probably the correct way to handle post-TGE airdrops going forward.

text:
日本退稅新制 11 月上路，現在已經有店家先用事後退稅，我是這樣用 AI 搞定的。

先講新制：以後是先付含稅價，離境時在海關辦退稅。唐吉訶德也宣布手續費 0 円，所以這陣子很多人在討論。

但我這趟遇到的是：即使同一個商場裡，每家店的退稅方式都不一樣。
有的店在櫃檯當場免稅。
有的店要事後在線上登記。

然而，我完全懶得研究這些。

我這趟的做法，全丟給grok bot:
1. Grok bot會帶到JPrefund做第一次設定，拍護照、自拍、登記退稅用的信用卡，只做一次。（2分鐘）
2. 之後每次買東西，把收據拍給 AI，它幫我查收據、判斷這家店退稅了沒？沒退的會直接去網站登記。￼

要說ai 真的改變了很多需要高度客製化的服務
對我最大的就是旅遊、健康（這我之後寫一篇文章）、教育（這我還在努力調整）

旅行上，以往的旅行社節省了旅行時食、住、行、法規的溝通成本。

而這塊，ai agent ( grok bot /muse)都能處理

（幫你訂機票、住宿、找當地評價網站好的餐廳幫你訂位）

而帶家人旅遊，相較於住五星飯店，我更愛住偏遠的民宿體驗當地，民宿會有很多麻煩的細節。

grok bot 幫你處理了訂房、民宿房主不管是紙本、dropbox的入住須知。ai都會讀完整理給你，有問題直接用當地語言傳訊息給房東。

家庭旅遊狀況很多，他會同時給予ABC旅遊方案，讓你容易調整。（而且是隨時）

這次最讓我驚艷到的，是他竟然還可以自己打電話去取消餐廳，主動提醒我要訂飛機兒童餐（還幫我訂）￼

旅程更像一個私人導遊在帶的感覺，當然細膩度還沒那麼高。有些地方要調教（整體80分）

但相較傳統高級旅行團，ai有它特殊的優勢。他更懂我，懂我家庭狀況。畢竟我們對話更多。我討厭網紅景點，它就帶我去一些只有當地人知道的景點。（他是根據當地人的評價）

很多時候你會感受到他的用心。（小孩喜歡吃什麼他都記得，會知道這店家你該點什麼）這樣以後去一些什麼要葡萄牙語、非洲語的自由行更能嘗試了。

Japan's new tax-refund system starts Nov 1. On this trip I handed the whole refund process to an AI (Grok Bot)
• New rule: pay the tax-inclusive price first, then get refunded at customs when you leave. Don Quijote waives its refund-application fee (cash pickup at the airport excluded)
• Reality: even inside one mall, some shops give tax-free at the counter and others need you to register online afterward
• My setup: one-time, about 2 minutes: passport photo, selfie, the card for refunds. After that I just photograph each receipt
• The AI works out whether the shop already refunded the tax, and registers it on the website if not
• Same for the whole trip: flights, lodging, well-reviewed local restaurants with bookings, and it reads the host's check-in guide and messages the host in Japanese for me
• For family trips it gives me Plan A, B and C at once, so I can switch any time
• Biggest surprise: it phoned a restaurant in Japanese to handle a cancellation, and it reminded me to order kids' meals on the flight, then booked them
• It feels like a private tour guide. About 80/100, still needs tuning, but it knows my family

他用 AI 做交易，一年赚了 98 亿美元，平均每天 2700 万美元，去年英国富豪榜第 20，今年冲到第 8

这人叫 Alex Gerko，46 岁，数学博士，公司里一个交易员都没有

AI 在他这儿只干一件事，猜接下来几秒到十几分钟，这个价格会往上走还是往下走

听着简单，可这件事极难，因为价格动一下之前，市场里会留下一堆蛛丝马迹，订单进来的速度、买单卖单的比例、某个价格上挂了多少货、谁在撤单，人脑根本来不及看，AI 能同时盯几万个品种

猜准了他怎么变成钱呢，他在每个品种上同时挂一个买价和一个卖价，模型说接下来要涨，他就把买价挂高一点、卖价收一点，模型说要跌，就反过来

成交之后他赚的是买价和卖价之间那条缝，可他手上也会多出一堆货，涨的还好，跌的就得马上想办法处理掉，要么在别的地方对冲，要么把报价往反方向偏，让下一个人赶紧把它接走

所以谁能活下来，看的是模型平均比对手准那么一点点，准得不多也没关系，他一天做几千万笔，一点点乘以几千万笔就是几十亿美元

Ok so a Ledger bought from an official European reseller contained a spy implant - complete with red wires and an antenna marked “欧亚版” (Eurasian version). It’s an older, cruder generation, yet it still made it through the official channel weeks ago…

The problem is no longer “one bad reseller in Asia.” 

Attackers are producing region-specific cellular implants and getting them into legitimate distribution. Ledger’s Genuine Check still passes because the secure element itself is authentic; the implant simply watches the screen and exfiltrates the seed.

Software checks are no longer enough.

PSA the ledger incident isn't limited to Asia

This is a device purchased in store from an official reseller in Europe (a legitimate device doesn't have any of these cables as can be seen in picture 2)

This even seems to be an old version of the 'spy implant' even though the device was purchased a couple of weeks ago. The newer versions usually hide the implant by the screen so it's easier to miss

What's interesting is that this compromised ledger never transfered funds to an exploiter. Either the device didn't work or they were waiting for a more widespread usage of the comprised devices? 

If you own a ledger that didn't directly come from the ledger online store make sure to not just rely on the software genuinely check by ledger but to actually open up the ledger yourself to make sure its original, again there are reported cases in Asia, south America and now Europe as well.

text:
thank you everyone for your participation and support through papertrade's launch.

we flipped the stock market’s volume in the first 6 hours. one day after launch, papertrade is a fully working 1000x exchange with 5m in the LP and has paid out 25M to stakers.

addressing two points that have come up:

-it was never possible to allow small notional to have the same priority as large notional. it opens the frontend up to spam congestion, which would have been infinitely worse than the existing queue. we designed the fair launch to be as inclusive as possible given those constraints.

-speaking of constraints, the overnight manipulation attempts on btc/eth on the hl bbo were not an oversight in the mechanism design we spent six months working on. these were always accounted for and only possible because the oi caps were extremely permissive for launch congestion. any oi cap during the queued launch demand would have exacerbated the slow experience, and the queue itself provided a natural protection against manipulation as confirming opens/closes had non-deterministic timing. as the congestion rolled off, we began the process of tightening up oi caps both onchain and at the relayer level. in a system like this, a manipulation attack is always possible - whether economically advantageous to attempt is the question. our goal is to set the parameters such that it is almost never profitable, and that the risk is extremely high/-EV at the tail even when it does work. evidence of this can be seen in the user that won overnight and continued to try again, ultimately donating almost all his profit back to the house via new accounts, without accounting for the cost of manipulating the bbo on hyperliquids side. a number of users equally opted to "undo" their manipulated trades in exchange for their farmed paper.

we are proud to be the first through the wall with this mechanism, at scale, in an adversarial environment. the market parameters cannot give undue advantage to either house or trader, such that the system becomes unstable and we have thought about these risks continuously since we began on this journey.

good luck to us.
